articles.headline: World Series 2026: 10 wild stats from the Brewers' first title
keyFacts: The Milwaukee Brewers won the 2026 World Series by defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 for their first title in franchise history.
The Brewers relied heavily on a dominant bullpen, which covered 55.1 percent of their postseason innings with a 1.38 ERA.
Catcher William Contreras won World Series MVP after posting strong offensive and defensive numbers throughout the postseason.
body: The Milwaukee Brewers are your 2026 World Series champions, having capped off a dominant postseason with a 4-1 win over the Tampa Bay Rays on Wednesday .

It’s a cathartic night for the Brewers, who were previously tied with the San Diego Padres as the oldest MLB team to have never won a World Series title. They are now permanently off that list , thanks to a team that leveraged its strengths all years.
How did the Brewers do it? Let’s dive into that via numbers.

We’re going to go ahead and list off every starting pitcher the Brewers faced in their 12 postseason games: Robbie Ray, Michael King, Nick Pivetta, Walker Buehler, Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Nick Martinez, Drew Rasmussen and Freddy Peralta.

That his a formidable group, even by playoff standards. Combined, they have 15 total All-Star appearances (and five Cy Young awards) compared to the Brewers rotation’s two, both by Jacob Misiorowski. And even Misiorowski’s first All-Star appearance last year was a matter of some controversy .
Would you like to know how long that group lasted against the Brewers lineup on average?

It’s 4.2 innings. Only one pitcher lasted longer than five innings at all and it was surprisingly Snell, despite the Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander being infamous for short starts even while posting zeroes.

The Brewers chased nearly every pitcher they faced this postseason by doing what they did all regular season. No team swung less at pitches. No team drew more walks. Only two teams in MLB missed less often when they did swing. They hit the most ground balls and the most balls to the opposite field.
They didn’t hit home runs much, ranking only 29th in MLB, but that entire previous paragraph turned their offense into a torture device for even some of MLB’s best pitchers.

Funnily enough, the Brewers starters lasted just as long as those opponents this postseason at 4.2 innings per start, but for very different reasons (and that number goes up to 4.5 when you take out Shane Drohan’s one-inning appearance as an opener).
The Brewers starters were definitely solid this postseason, but Milwaukee removed them as early as possible in basically every game and roll out its comically dominant bullpen.
The Brewers relievers pitched 65 innings this postseason and posted a 1.38 ERA and a .173 batting average against, per MLB.com’s Sarah Langs .
That was the Brewers’s formula when you zoom out as much as possible: force the other team’s starter out early and turn the game into a battle of the bullpens. It worked to perfection.
Jacob Misiorowski was still the Brewers ace in the postseason. AP Photo/Ashley Landis

There’s something to be said, though, about what that means for baseball. The starting pitcher who regularly goes seven innings or more in a start is bordering on extinction. Sandy Alcantara led all pitchers with 214 innings during the regular season, which would have ranked for ninth in MLB 10 years ago and 22nd in MLB 20 years ago.
Teams are now perfectly willing to accept a five-inning start, if it means those are five good innings. This has been a slow shift in MLB for years, but the Brewers just brought it into sharp focus.
That’s the proportion of innings the Brewers bullpen covered during the postseason.
That makes Milwaukee the fourth champion in MLB history to get a majority of its innings from relievers, joining the 2020 Los Angeles Dodgers, 2021 Atlanta Braves and 2024 Dodgers.

It had never happened before 2020, another sign of the aggressive-bullpen era. The closest any team ever got before that was the 1960 Pittsburgh Pirates, though that was hardly a conscious decision. That team took three double-digit losses to the New York Yankees before winning in seven games, with relievers forced to cover for short starts in each defeat.
That is the number of home runs hit in the 2026 World Series, per ESPN , the fewest since the 1985 Fall Classic between the Kansas City Royals and St. Louis Cardinals.
The Brewers had three of those homers, from perhaps the three players you would least expect: Sal Frelick, Cooper Pratt and David Hamilton, the No. 6, 7 and 9 hitters in the Game 5 lineup.
The Brewers built their offense around not needing homers to punish pitchers, but they still out-homered the competition in every round, with a total margin of 13 to 4.
In another world, the 2026 World Series ends in Game 4 on Tuesday as a Brewers sweep and rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt gets remembered as the guy who homered his club to its first title.

A 12th-inning collapsed prevented that from coming to pass, but it did give the 22-year-old a chance to make some history. With two more hits in Game 5, Pratt became the first rookie to post a base hit in six straight at-bats in the World Series .
Cooper Pratt has a hit in 6 straight at-bats 🤯
This is the most by a rookie in the World Series! pic.twitter.com/MTicuHxMDP
— MLB (@MLB) October 29, 2026

Pratt made his MLB debut in June and was playing high school baseball only three years ago, with the Brewers taking him in the sixth round of the 2023 MLB Draft. He rocketed to the majors thanks to his well-regarded glove, then made his mark with his bat.
With a single in the seventh inning, Brewers star Jackson Chourio became MLB’s all-time leader in postseason hits before turning 23, breaking a tie with Andruw Jones with his 31st hit.

Jones posted his 30 hits in 45 games for the Atlanta Braves. Chourio posted his 31 in 25 games. He also tied some guy named Babe Ruth for the most hits in the first four games of a World Series , and now has the second-most in five games behing only Pepper Martin in 1931 .
You would think with either of the above stats, Pratt or Chourio would have been named World Series MVP. It’s a sign of how thoroughly great William Contreras was that neither were.

Contreras earned MVP after a postseason in which he was basically the best player in baseball. The three-time All-Star slashed .373/.448/.588 at the plate during the postseason. He threw out 6-of-13 baserunners. And he won won 21 out of 31 ABS challenges (67.8%) in the first postseason with the system, with accuracy and decisiveness becoming a running joke in the Fox Sports booth.
In the World Series, Contreras hit 8-for-21 (.381) with four RBI, including one on a double in Game 5.
What else could you possible want from a catcher?
Misiorowski began the World Series by throwing the fastest pitch in its tracked history at 103.5 mph . He would go on to throw 89 pitches of at least 100 mph between his starts in Games 1 and 5.

Misiorowski didn’t reach the end of the sixth inning in either start — exiting Game 5 due to calf cramps — but he allowed only one run in 10 2/3 total innings. His five strikeouts were lower than his regular season norm, but he was still an ace by Brewers standards.

Aaron Ashby went from a relatively anonymous set-up man to the most feared reliever in baseball over the course of the postseason, making nine appearances in 12 games and pitching multiple innings in all but one.

The left-hander didn’t allow a single run in his 18 innings pitched, the most innings a reliever has ever thrown in a postseason without giving up a run . He didn’t factor into Game 5 after experiencing diminished velocity in a long Game 4 appearance, but he had already contributed more than enough.
$142 million
There will be plenty of analysis about what it means the Brewers — a classic small-market, big-brain team — winning the World Series means for baseball.

Their $142 million payroll, as estimated by Roster Resource , ranked 19th in MLB this season, right between the Kansas City Royals and Cincinnati Reds. They were actually the financial heavyweight this series, as the Rays ranked 28th at $90 million, followed by their ALCS opponent Cleveland Guardians at $87 million.

You build a champion on that budget with smart decisions and long-term planning. The highest-paid player on the 2026 Brewers was Christian Yelich ($26 million), still playing on the mega-deal he got from his MVP days, followed by the mostly injured Brandon Woodruff ($22 million) and two trade deadline acquisitions in Dustin May and Antonio Senzatela ($12 million each).

No other player on the Brewers made more than $10 million this year. Chourio and Pratt, both 22-year-olds who just starred on a World Series team, are both under team control through at least 2031, at the cost of around $132 million.

Conteras will be back next year on a $14.5 million club option. Nearly every other big contributor is under contract beyond 2027, save for NLCS MVP Jake Bauers, a pending free agent. And let’s not forget the Brewers still ranked third in MLB Pipeline’s farm system rankings after the trade deadline , with a group headlined by No. 1 overall prospect Jesús Made.
The Brewers were incredible this year. There is every reason to believe they will stay incredible for years to come.

articles.headline: History! MLS sets new single-season goals record in 2026
keyFacts: Major League Soccer set a new single-season goals record on Wednesday night in 2026.
Lucas Halter scored the record-breaking 1,553rd goal of the season during a match between the Houston Dynamo FC and Seattle Sounders FC.
The new record surpassed the previous mark of 1,552 goals set in 2024, with two more Matchdays remaining in the season.
body: History! MLS sets new single-season goals record in 2026 By MLSsoccer staff
Major League Soccer is the league of goals, with the likes of Lionel Messi , Petar Musa and other lighting up opposing nets game in and game out.
That has especially been the case in 2026, as MLS set a new single-season goals record on Wednesday night.
Lucas Halter did the honors by scoring the 1,553rd goal of the season - surpassing the previous mark of 1,552 set in 2024 - during Houston Dynamo FC 's 1-0 win at Seattle Sounders FC .
Several more goals followed on the night, and with two more Matchdays to go, this year's record may last for the foreseeable future.
But as the league of goals™, MLS will be sure to make it interesting next season and beyond.

articles.headline: Israel election: Netanyahu-led bloc holds lead with nearly 90% of votes counted
keyFacts: Partial Israeli election results show Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc leading with 53 seats, while Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc holds 48 seats.
Neither bloc is projected to secure the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member Knesset.
President Isaac Herzog said he will begin consultations next week with party factions to form a government.
body: What you need to know
- Israel's election turnout was the highest in decades
- Latest vote count at 90% shows Netanyahu's Likud-led bloc holding the lead at 53 seats
- Anti-Netanyahu bloc led by Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot at 48 seats
- At least 61 seats are needed to form a secure majority
- Neither party is expected to win an outright majority, with difficult coalition talks expected in the weeks ahead
Follow below for all the latest on the Israeli election
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google. Then tap the "Star" or "Preferred" to keep DW News at the top of your feed.
UN rights chief: Next government should 'change course massively'
The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, told reporters in New York that he hopes a new Israeli government will "change course massively" and respect international law.

"The message is: don't continue the current course of warfare where you think you are above international law, because I think that's what we have frankly seen in the current environment," Türk said, as relayed by the AFP news agency.

"Israel has its obligations under international law, international humanitarian law, international human rights law, and they need to respect them," he said. "And I hope that the next government will do precisely that and change course massively."
Türk also said in a statement on Monday that Israel's operation in recent days in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron raised serious concerns about "unnecessary and disproportionate" use of force.
He said that more than 2,000 people had been displaced, with homes and commercial property destroyed and free movement impeded by the lockdown.
"Collective punishment is a grave violation of international law," Türk said. "Threats to empty and erase entire neighborhoods also raise serious concerns of ethnic cleansing."
'Arab Israelis have trusted democracy,' Greens' Omid Nouripour tells DW
Omid Nouripour, one of the deputy speakers in Germany's Bundestag parliament, has told DW that the high turnout in Israel was a testament to the strength of the country's democracy.

"For now, of course, we do not know what the coalition-building will look like, but the people have put their trust in democracy," Nouripour said. "Above all, Arab Israelis have trusted democracy and gone to the polls in droves."

Speaking to DW's Rosalia Romaniec, as he accompanies German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier on his state visit to China, Nouripour also said that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's and other right-wing parties' religiously-charged campaign strategy appeared to have backfired.

"This big campaign from Netanyahu's camp, first and foremost against the Arab Israelis, has on the one hand mobilized people to such an extent that there is no longer a majority for this camp," he said.
Nouripour, a former Green party co-leader, has been a Bundestag member for 20 years. Born in Tehran, his family moved from Iran to Germany when he was a teenager.
WATCH: Early Israeli election results point to deadlock

Israel's election has produced no clear winner, leaving both Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot short of a path to power. Israel could now be facing weeks of political uncertainty.
IN DEPTH: What would a new Israeli government mean for Arab neighbors?
A new Israeli government is unlikely to bring big changes on controversial topics like Palestinian statehood and Israeli troops in Lebanon and Syria, experts say.
Some small positives may be possible though.
Read DW's full report on what might change for Arab countries after Israel's election.
GRAPHIC — Knesset seats by party, and by bloc
Election commission says almost half a million 'double envelope' ballots still to be counted
The Central Elections Commission (CEC) estimates that there are still between 430,000 and 480,000 so-called "double envelope" ballots to count, according to Israeli media.
These are cast primarily by soldiers, prisoners and diplomats stationed abroad, as well as others unable to vote at their designated polling stations.
This estimate is lower than the CEC's previous prediction of around 600,000 but it remains subject to change.
Such ballots are still being received and processed, and officials also have to double-check that the individuals sending them in have not also voted at a physical polling station on election day.
Because of these complications, they tend to be among the last votes to be counted.
A full vote count is tentatively expected by tomorrow afternoon, although the official finalized results will only follow on November 4.

If the CEC's estimated range is roughly correct, this group of ballots would equate to not very far shy of 10% of the total number of votes cast. As such, they have at least the theoretical potential to impact the seat distribution quite considerably.
President Herzog says it's imperative 'to avoid another round of elections'

President Isaac Herzog, who will have a key role in choosing someone to try to put together the next government, has urged all parties to "come with an open mind" when the time for negotiations comes.

"I will receive the official election results next week," Herzog said. "I wil then begin the process of the consultations here, hearing from each and every fraction, asking questions, and holding discussions."

Typically the president chooses the leader of the party with the most votes to try to form a government although he is not required to follow this convention. That nominee then has 42 days to try to set up a working coalition.

"One thing must be clear, and I said this before the elections too," Herzog said. "We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections. So I expect everyone who comes here to come with an open mind."
Between April 2019 and November 2022, Israel had five general elections in rather rapid succession amid similar difficulties either forming or maintaining coalition governments.
Situation barely moves as more than 80% of vote counted

Partial results published by the Central Elections Committee and reported by the Times of Israel newspaper showed the bloc led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on 54 seats, with 84.5% of votes counted.
The opposition bloc under Gadi Eisenkot of the centrist Yashar party was on 49 seats.
Neither bloc is set to receive the 61 seats need for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, making some form of coalition likely.
The Arab-led parties — the Joint List and the United Arab List, commonly known under its Hebrew name of Ra'am — have dropped to 17 seats.
The numbers are still likely to change, particularly after a record number of absentee votes are counted.
The full tally of those will possibly not be confirmed until Friday, according to the newspaper.
Arab list leader calls for Jewish-Arab partnership to oust Netanyahu
The leader of the far-left Joint List, one of Israel's Arab-majority lists, has called for a "genuine Jewish-Arab partnership" to help remove Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

"Anyone who wants to offer a substantive and genuine alternative to Netanyahu's blood-soaked government will have to talk to us to secure the path to the change that the public in Israel longs for," Yousef Jabareen told Israeli media.
"We will know how to use our political strength to advance the values we believe in," Jabareen said.
"We are ready to pave the way for the replacement of the government of Netanyahu, Ben-Gvir and [Finance Minister Bezalel] Smotrich — and send them home."
After most votes have been counted from Tuesday's election, the conservative Islamist Ra'am party and the Joint List are projected to win a combined 19 seats in the 120-member Knesset.

As neither the pro-Netanyahu bloc nor the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot seem likely to win a majority, the Arab parties could play a key role in the formation of the next government.
Right-wing Jewish parties in Israel have traditionally refused to cooperate with Arab parties, and Netanyahu said on Wednesday doing so would be "treasonous."
However, at least one opposition party is open to the idea, with the leader of the left-leading Democrats, Yair Golan, saying Wednesday he supported bringing Arab-led parties into a coalition.
Little shift in numbers as three-quarters of votes tallied

Partial results issued by the Central Elections Committee and cited by the Times of Israel showed little movement in results with 76.8% of votes counted, with the pro-Netanyahu bloc on 54 seats and the anti-Netanyahu bloc on 47.
However, the United Arab List, commonly known by its Hebrew abbreviation Ra'am, saw a gain of two seats, bringing the Arab parties to 19.
The results will change as counting progresses.
Both main blocs remain short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset.
Left-wing leader calls for 'courage' to unite with Arab parties
Yair Golan, the head of Israel's main left-wing party, the Democrats, has called on partners in the opposition alliance to be ready to work with Arab parties to gain a majority and take government.
"We must no longer accept [Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu's racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes," he said on X.
"We have a responsibility. And we have an opportunity to form a government of change in partnership with Israel's Arab citizens," he wrote.

Arab parties have around 16 seats amid the ongoing count, while the anti-Netanyahu bloc under former military chief Gadi Eisenkot is on around 48, meaning that a coalition between them would produce the necessary majority in the Knesset.
Netanyahu's bloc had some 56 seats after around two-thirds of votes had been counted.
Several opposition parties have so far rejected working together with the Arab parties.
Netanyahu bloc holds slight lead after more than half of votes counted: elections committee

Partial results issued by Israel's Central Elections Committee and reported by the Times of Israel after 57.3% of votes were counted have shown the pro-Netanyahu bloc with a projected 55 seats, seven seats ahead of the anti-Netanyahu bloc with 49.
Neither side so far has the 61 seats needed to form a secure majority and are not expected to do so.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party currently leads with a projected 27 seats, with challenger Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party coming in at 21 seats projected.
Arab parties so far are projected to win 15 seats.
The Likud and Yashar parties are leading their respective blocs.
These are partial results that will change as counting progresses.
In particular, the special votes cast by people outside their assigned polling stations, such as those of soldiers, are counted later.
A record 650,000 such absentee votes are expected this year, equivalent to around 14 seats in the Knesset.
This means the absentee votes could markedly affect the final election result, the Israel Hayom newspaper reported.
Netanyahu calls for 'strong' right-wing government after election
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to form a new right-wing government, despite exit polls showing no clear majority for either political bloc.
"We are still waiting for the real results," Netanyahu told cheering supporters in a speech early Wednesday, stressing that his Likud party was the largest in Israel.
"We must put in place a strong government of the right," he said.
Netanyahu also rejected the prospect of a government relying on the support of Arab parties, which made strong gains in Tuesday's election.
Turning to security, Netanyahu said Israel had a "unique opportunity" together with US President Donald Trump to end what he called the Iranian threat.

Updated exit polls show Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot either tied or separated by a narrow margin. Neither side is projected to win the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset.
Updated exit polls show Netanyahu and opposition blocs neck and neck
Updated Israeli exit polls suggest Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc is now tied with the opposition, after earlier projections showed a narrow lead for the bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot.

Public broadcaster Kan 11 and Channel 13 both put the pro-Netanyahu and anti-Netanyahu blocs at 51 seats each. Channel 12, meanwhile, is now showing the pro-Netanyahu camp with an edge at 52 seats and the opposition at 49 seats.
Kan 11's latest projection gives Netanyahu's Likud party 27 seats, up from 25 in its earlier poll.
However, none of the three major networks project either bloc winning the 61 seats needed for a majority in Israel's 120-seat parliament, the Knesset.
Eisenkot calls on Netanyahu to resign in post-election speech
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has called on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to step down, saying voters have sent a clear message that they want change.
"We've made history," Eisenkot told supporters in a speech in Jerusalem following Tuesday's election. "The public voted against the continuation of Netanyahu as prime minister."
He said a "decent leader" would accept the public's will and announce his resignation, warning that another round of elections would be a mistake.
Eisenkot pledged to work towards forming what he called a "Zionist conscription government," referring to his push for broader military service obligations.
"We would like to represent all Israelis," he said, adding that the country needed stable leadership and a government that represented all parts of society.
The former military chief also warned Netanyahu against making major security decisions or launching new wars, arguing that he no longer had a mandate to do so.
"Netanyahu: Don't you dare use Israel's security for your political needs," Eisenkot said.

articles.headline: Can Turkiye’s Libya breakthrough reshape Eastern Mediterranean diplomacy?
keyFacts: Libya's eastern parliament approved a 2019 maritime agreement with Turkiye, reversing years of opposition to the deal.
Greece, Cyprus, and Egypt argue the agreement infringes on their sovereign rights, while Turkiye claims it complies with international law.
Turkiye and Egypt will conduct a joint naval exercise in Alexandria from November 4 to 9, Turkish officials announced.
body: Istanbul, Turkiye – Once adversaries, Turkiye and the leadership of eastern Libya are now building closer political and military ties. Ankara has also repaired relations with Egypt in the past few years after previous hostility, but a maritime dispute is testing how far those reconciliations can go.

On Wednesday, Turkiye’s Ministry of National Defence renewed its offer to sign a maritime boundary agreement with Cairo, arguing that Egypt could gain more than 15,000sq km (5,790sq miles) of maritime jurisdiction – a figure that is Ankara’s estimate – compared with a potential further agreement with Greece, with which Cairo signed a partial maritime deal in 2020.

The offer came eight days after Libya’s eastern-based parliament in Tobruk reversed years of opposition and approved a maritime agreement signed between its rival, the internationally recognised government based in the Libyan capital, Tripoli, and Turkiye in 2019.

The agreement delineates maritime jurisdiction areas claimed by Turkiye and Libya in the Mediterranean, but Greece, Cyprus and Egypt argued that it infringes on their sovereign rights while Turkiye maintains that it complies with international law.
A senior Turkish official told Al Jazeera that eastern Libya’s leaders had come to recognise Ankara’s intentions.
“Turkiye is not there to use Libya for its own purposes,” the official said.
“From the very beginning, we have supported a policy of one Libya,” the official added, stressing that the country’s stability and resources should benefit all Libyans.
From confrontation to cooperation

Turkiye helped repel a 2019-2020 offensive on Tripoli by forces loyal to renegade military commander Khalifa Haftar, leader of the military forces of the eastern government. Ankara has since expanded its relations with the eastern camp while maintaining ties with Tripoli.
The senior official said Turkish security personnel based in Tripoli had remained in contact with eastern Libyan forces even during the confrontation.
“There has actually been no change in our policy. Only the results it has produced have changed,” the official said.
The diplomatic outreach has been accompanied by military and intelligence contacts.
In May, Defence Minister Yasar Guler met Saddam Haftar, Khalifa Haftar’s son, and Abdulsalam al-Zoubi, a senior defence official in the Tripoli-based government.
Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin also met Saddam Haftar in Benghazi on June 23. Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan followed in August, meeting both Khalifa and Saddam Haftar.

A change in Libya’s eastern parliamentary leadership also preceded the maritime vote. On October 6, lawmakers replaced Aguila Saleh as parliament speaker with Al-Salhin Abdelnabi al-Obeidi, who previously chaired the Libyan-Turkish parliamentary friendship committee.
Galip Dalay, a senior research fellow at Chatham House, sees Ankara’s engagement with its former adversaries as a strategic gain.
“This is not merely a pragmatic or tactical gain. It is a strategic gain for Turkiye,” he told Al Jazeera.
Dalay argued that closer relations with both Libyan camps make it harder to establish Eastern Mediterranean energy and security arrangements that exclude Turkiye.
What does eastern Libya gain?
The rapprochement also reflects political calculations within the Haftar camp.

Tarek Megerisi, a visiting fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, believes Saddam Haftar hopes Ankara’s influence could strengthen his own political prospects with many believing that he eventually wants to lead Libya.
The senior Turkish official said Ankara had made no specific political commitments to eastern Libyan officials beyond general principles and cooperation that would also benefit Libya.

Representatives of both Libyan camps held talks in Ankara on Friday about unifying their military structures, according to Libyan media reports. Differences over political oversight remain unresolved, and no final agreement has been announced.
But Anas El Gomati, director of the Sadeq Institute, cautioned that an understanding between Libya’s rival leaders would not necessarily produce an inclusive political settlement.
“An elite bargain between two camps can leave out everyone beyond them,” he said.
Egypt: The diplomatic balancing act
The Libyan eastern parliament’s reversal has also complicated Egypt’s position. Cairo has traditionally supported the eastern leadership but opposes the maritime agreement it has now endorsed.
On October 22, Greek Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis announced discussions with Egypt on extending their partial 2020 maritime delimitation agreement eastwards towards Cyprus.
Four days later, Egypt joined Greece, Cyprus, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and the European Union in a statement at the United Nations rejecting the Turkiye-Libya accord.
Yet Cairo and Ankara have continued rebuilding their relationship.

Turkiye’s land forces commander, General Metin Tokel, arrived in Egypt on Monday for an official visit. The Turkish Defence Ministry has also announced a joint naval exercise in Alexandria from November 4 to 9.
The senior Turkish official told Al Jazeera that Ankara remained open to cooperation on maritime boundaries and energy but would defend what it considers its rights.
“Just as other countries say they will not give up the rights they recognise as their own, the same applies to Turkiye,” the official said.

Fidan has acknowledged Egypt’s concerns and discussed the possibility of cooperation with Italy. The official clarified, however, that no formal four-country negotiating mechanism between Turkiye, Libya, Italy and Egypt has been established.
El Gomati believes Cairo’s ability to influence decisions in eastern Libya has diminished.
“Egypt still has influence, but it no longer has a veto,” he said.

Megerisi, meanwhile, argued that Turkiye’s relationship with Egypt has become too important to sacrifice over the maritime dispute. He sees room for accommodation, potentially involving Italy’s energy company Eni, which has interests in Egypt and Libya.
A breakthrough with limits

Greece maintains that the maritime agreement disregards the rights of its islands, including Crete. Turkiye rejects those claims, arguing that islands should not automatically receive the same weight as mainland coastlines when mapping out maritime boundaries and exclusive economic zones.

Megerisi said the eastern Libyan parliament’s approval strengthens the agreement’s domestic legal footing but does little to resolve the wider dispute between the countries of the Eastern Mediterranean.
“I think both sides are maximalist,” he said.
The parliamentary vote gives Ankara greater political leverage, but it does not settle competing maritime claims or clear the way for offshore energy exploration.

Ankara now wants to build on its gains in Libya and improving ties with Egypt to strengthen its position in the Eastern Mediterranean. Its aim is to develop new partnerships and regional cooperation rather than remain outside arrangements shaped largely by Greece, Cyprus and Israel.
But that will require finding common ground with countries that continue to challenge Turkiye’s maritime claims.
The senior Turkish official said Ankara’s improved relationship with Cairo had opened the door to discussing those differences directly.
“We can now discuss every issue with Egypt, and we will discuss this one too,” the official said. “We do not have to seek the approval or consent of unrelated third countries.”

articles.headline: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon looks like a diamond in the rough
keyFacts: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, a new AI model priced temporarily at two dollars per million input tokens and ten dollars per million output tokens.
Google DeepMind SVP Koray Kavukcuoglu stated that Carbon excels in cybersecurity and long-running tasks, achieving higher benchmark scores than its predecessor Argon.
Google will release the Carbon model this week to select cybersecurity defenders and plans to make it more broadly available later.
body: Just two weeks after launching Gemini 4 Argon, Google has announced a better-performing version of the model that it will sell for the same price, at least temporarily.

Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP at Google DeepMind and chief AI architect at Google, said Gemini 4 Carbon represents the company's strongest model yet, particularly in terms of cybersecurity and long-running tasks.

There's some irony in the name "Carbon", given the Chocolate Factory plans a carbon-dioxide-free future . Given Google's political timidity when it comes to names on maps , Gemini 4 Americium might be more representative of management's worldview. Gemini 4 Silicon is another missed opportunity — the chemical symbol is Si, a bobbleheaded nod to "Super Intelligence."

Priced initially at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, Gemini 4 Carbon sells for the same amount as its predecessor Argon during an indeterminate introductory period. When that period expires, Google will lift prices to $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens.
That's the same as Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, which Google clearly sees as Carbon's competition.
Last month, Google's ability to compete in the wake of the leadership change at its DeepMind AI subsidiary looked less certain .

But Carbon has posted impressive benchmark scores, taking the lead in SEC-bench Pro, ExploitGym, and CWE-bench, while landing at fourth place on WebDev Arena , behind Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Astra, and Sonnet 5.5. Carbon currently ranks second, behind Opus 5.5, in Arena.ai's leaderboard for Best Overall Agent.

Model ratings biz Artificial Analysis says Google's new model tops its newly formulated Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 and comes in second to Claude Code Opus 5.5 on its Coding Agent Index.

Kavukcuoglu emphasized Carbon's cybersecurity capabilities, which will be available this week to an unspecified set of cybersecurity defenders and more eventually through the company's Fairwind access program. "On internal benchmarks, Carbon achieves more than 2x uplift in success rate for generating secure code over Argon," he wrote. "As another example, the Chrome team has reported that Carbon performed more than 10x better than another lab's large frontier model when generating high quality patches."

"Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon are now leading at the frontier," said Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, in a statement [PDF] accompanying Alphabet's Q3 2026 earnings. "Overall, our first-party model APIs are now processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, more than four times what we processed a year ago."

While Google may hope to surpass Anthropic and OpenAI in terms of model performance and usage, it's already ahead in revenue. Pointing to the company's strong Q3 earnings, Emarketer principal analyst Nate Elliott in a statement told The Register , "In a sly nod to the way AI-only companies talk about their revenue, Google bragged about its half-trillion dollar run rate – almost ten times more than either OpenAI or Anthropic."
Google will release Carbon this week to select cybersecurity defenders. The company aims to make the AI model more broadly available "as soon as possible." ®

articles.headline: Yaxel Lendeborg is ready to reignite his newfound rivalry with Luka Doncic
keyFacts: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg started a rivalry with Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic during his first NBA game.
The Los Angeles Lakers and the Golden State Warriors are scheduled to play against each other again on Friday.
Yaxel Lendeborg stated that he is ready for the upcoming matchup against Luka Doncic on Friday.
body: To start the 2026-27 NBA season, Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg ignited a rivalry with Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Doncic. It was a big story because Lendeborg was not shy about talking trash to one of the league's best players.

Since that was his first-ever NBA game, it was even more impressive. Lendeborg has never been the type of player to back down from a challenge, and that has led to him playing so well in his rookie year so far. Now, he has another shot at Doncic, and it could be a golden opportunity.
Yaxel Lendeborg wants to keep challenging Luka Doncic
Doncic has been one of the best players in the league yet again this season. He is fresh off games where he scored 50+ points and 40+ points, which is a bad sign for anyone who wants to defend him.

On Friday, the Lakers and the Warriors will play against each other again. While Doncic had 28 points during their first matchup, Lendeborg did hold him to some inefficient numbers when he was matched up against him.

Since that game, Lendeborg has also been superb to start his NBA career. In his first five games, Lendeborg has averaged 22.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, and four assists per game. He definitely has shown that he is ready for the big leagues, and that involves him playing against stars like Doncic.

articles.headline: Fox News Host Gives JD Vance Some Tough Love About His 2028 Prospects
keyFacts: Fox News analyst Brit Hume argued that JD Vance's close alliance with Donald Trump could be a liability in the 2028 primary.
Vice President JD Vance admitted that receiving Donald Trump's endorsement for the 2028 presidential race is not a foregone conclusion.

body: Fox News host Brian Kilmeade doesn’t seem particularly optimistic about the idea of Vice President JD Vance becoming the GOP’s candidate in 2028.

On Wednesday’s “Brian Kilmeade Show” with fellow Fox News personality Brit Hume, the pair discussed whether connections to President Donald Trump would help or hurt in 2028. Hume contended that Vance’s alliance with Trump could work against him come primary season.

“A lot depends on how the public and the party feel about Donald Trump by the time 2028 rolls around,” Hume said. “And if you’re as attached to the hip to Trump as indeed Vance is, it’s a good question whether that’s a liability or a benefit. I think it might end up being a liability.”
Kilmeade’s view of Vance’s future in the 2028 race was less than rosy.
Vance admitted earlier this month that Trump’s endorsement wasn’t a foregone conclusion.

“I think that Trump’s endorsement just carries more weight than any political endorsement in history, because of that, obviously, the voters are gonna decide. Donald Trump is only one vote of many, but I think his endorsement is still the most powerful,” Vance told Mark Halperin.
Trump recently dodged a question about endorsing Vance.
“Well, I tell you this, he’s a very talented person, and he’s a very good person, but we’ve, literally, I don’t think we’ve ever talked about it,” Trump said.

articles.headline: 15 Years Later, the Most Near-Perfect Fast and Furious Movie Is Getting From Netflix
keyFacts: The 2011 action film Fast Five is leaving Netflix on November 1 after streaming there all summer.
The movie marked a franchise shift from street racing to a heist plot in Rio de Janeiro.
Polygon stated that Fast Five remains the best film in the series due to its practical effects and balance.
body: For a long time, I assumed the Fast & Furious franchise were beneath me. The movies appeared to be nothing more than a series of vapid car commercials and, not being much of a car guy, I wasn't interested. But during the pandemic, I got pressured into watching the first one and really enjoyed it. Before I knew it, I’d watched every installment and couldn’t wait for the next one. That's the power of family.

Including the Hobbs & Shaw spinoff movie, there have been 11 Fast & Furious films to date, with a 12th and final one is on the way. While all of them have their moments, Fast Five, still remains the best for the way it repositioned the franchise, used all the best characters (including Paul Walker), and leaned on largely practical effects to take you along for the ride. Fast Five has been streaming on Netflix all summer, but as of Nov. 1 it will drive off into the sunset. So there's never been a better time to revisit this modern action classic.
How Fast & Furious got to Fast Five

Before Fast Five, the Fast & Furious movies were all about street racing. Vin Diesel’s Dominic Toretto was an illegal street racer and the other characters were his friends, family, and rivals. Paul Walker began as an LAPD officer who’d gone undercover to infiltrate the illegal streetracing scene. But then Walker’s character, Brian O'Conner, realized this street racing thing was pretty cool, and he fell in love with Dom’s sister, Mia (Jordana Brewster). So he becomes a street racer himself. (Brian later becomes an FBI agent, then goes bad again. Fast Five picks up after that second time.)

Fast Five was the first movie in the franchise not to focus on street racing. Instead, it’s a heist where Dominic and Brian, along with a full crew, plot to steal $100 million from a corrupt businessman so that they can start new lives. Meanwhile, as they’re hiding out in Rio de Janeiro (which is where most of the movie takes place), Dom, Brian, Mia and the others are being pursued by American DSS Agents for the murder of some DEA agents (which they were framed for by the businessman they’re plotting to steal from).

Before the big heist takes place, those DSS agents, lead by Luke Hobbs (Dwayne Johnson), capture Dom, Brian and a couple of other crew members. Then, Hobbs’ team is attacked by the businessman and Hobbs’ team dies, making Hobbs realize Dom and Brian (who saved him) are good dudes. He even helps them with the big heist, which famously involves two Dodge Chargers, driven by Dom and Brian, tethered to a giant bank vault being dragged through the streets of Rio. In the end, they essentially get away with it, becoming very rich fugitives.

What really makes this movie work is the fact that it’s a fairly simple heist story. White some of what I described above may seem convoluted, the plot is basically a bunch of outlaws plotting to steal money from a bad guy, making it easy to root for them.

In future movies, Dom’s team is repositioned as an elite spy team, called upon by the US government whenever a mission requires for a bunch of guys who can drive really fast. The future movies work and they’re still more exciting than the street racing stories, but after Fast Five the movies feel a bit more like Mission: Impossible. Fast Five finds the perfect balance where they’re still outlaw racers, but they happen to plan a heist because they hate this rich dude.

The Fast & Furious films have a lot of great characters. Dominic is a great lead and there are lots of fun characters in the crew that come and go in various films. Of course, one of the best characters is Walker’s Brian O’Connor. This is not only because Walker was charming in the role, but because Brian’s friendship with Dominic was the key relationship that shaped the series. That brotherhood gets cemented in Fast Five. It's the first time they’re both on the same side the whole time, and it's the one where Mia is revealed to be pregnant, making Dom and Brian actually family.

We get to see more of their friendship in the 6th and 7th movies, but with Walker’s death partway through Furious 7, some clunky editing was needed to keep him in the film (it’s done very well, but you can still feel how it was reworked mid-film). After that point, Brian is still alive in the Fast & Furious universe, but he’s decided to settle down with Mia and stays offscreen for the future installments. While the 8th, 9th and 10th movies that followed are all enjoyable, someone’s clearly missing.

The reason why people watch these movies is the action, and Fast Five has all the other films in the franchise beat. That vault heist, which was filmed in Puerto Rico doubling for Rio, involved lots of real-world destruction and car-smashing. While CG was used for some of it, a lot of the vault stuff was done with a drivable vault which smashed into all kinds of things.

After this film, as the crew got into more of the superspy stuff, the set pieces tended to transcend reality a good deal more. With that came even more reliance on CGI. Perhaps the most notorious example of this is the scene in F9 where a couple of characters essentially drive a car into space.

From what we know about the upcoming final film, Fast Forever, I’m willing to bet Fast Five stays the best movie. Recently, Vin Diesel laid out his three big demands for the final film, saying that it should return to Los Angeles, it should return to street racing, and it should involve the reunion of Dom and Brian. While I’m fine with going back to LA, the street racing thing kind of got old by the fourth film, which is why the movies needed to pivot in the first place. And, while Furious 7 managed to convincingly revive Paul Walker with the actors brothers as stand-ins and some CGI face replacement, I do not want to see him resurrected for another time as that kind of thing often feels gross and disrespectful. Worse, it would undermine the truly poetic work done in the seventh film to give Brian a proper sendoff.

With all due respect to Vin Diesel, I want a movie that follows the lessons from the best film in the franchise, Fast Five and the big lessons from that movie are that practical effects are way better than computer-generated ones and that street racing is, well, kinda lame.

articles.headline: Hegseth dismisses top military strategist from Joint Chiefs as Trump contemplates further Iran strikes
keyFacts: War Secretary Pete Hegseth dismissed Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia from his role as Joint Staff director of strategy, plans, and policy.
Sylvia's office provides plans, strategies, and policy recommendations to Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine to support national security.
President Donald Trump has publicly acknowledged he is considering further military strikes on Iran following next week's elections.
body: War Secretary Pete Hegseth ousted a top military strategist from the Joint Chiefs of Staff this week as President Donald Trump contemplates additional strikes on Iran following next week’s elections.
Hegseth fired Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, who was the director for strategy, plans and policy, J5, on the Joint Staff this week, the Atlantic reported.

“The Chairman, the Joint Staff, and the Joint Force extend our deepest gratitude to Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia and his family for their 32 years of distinguished service to our nation,” a spokesperson for the Joint Chiefs told the Washington Examiner . “We wish him and his family the best as they graduate to new opportunities and the next chapters of their lives.”
The spokesperson did not provide a reason for his dismissal. Sylvia’s predecessor, Army Lt. Gen. Joseph McGee, was forced to retire about a year ago.
Maj. Gen. Mark Slocum serves as the vice director for strategy, plans, and policy, J5.
The Joint Staff J5 offers plans, strategies, and policy recommendations to the chairman of the Joint Chiefs, currently Gen. Dan Caine, to further the national security interests of the country.

The firing comes as Trump has publicly acknowledged he’s considering his options for after next week’s elections regarding the Iran war. He could order a resumption of kinetic military strikes, though it’s unclear what goals the new operation could entail.

The war began over Iran’s nuclear program, but its deepest facility remains intact, and its enriched uranium is believed to still be buried underground following Operation Midnight Hammer. Shortly after the war began, Iran began attacking shipping vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, which severely reduced transits and caused the ongoing energy crisis.

Earlier this month, the Pentagon informed Congress that its latest tally showed the war in Iran has cost roughly $47.1 billion . Replacing expended munitions will cost roughly $29 billion, the largest chunk of that total.
THE MILITARY’S $1 BILLION DRONE PLAN TO TAKE ON CHINA — AND HOW IT HOPES IT NEVER HAS TO USE THEM

Hegseth, notably, has fired several senior military leaders during his tenure, most often without explanation. Some of those firings have raised bipartisan concerns. Hegseth said last month he had fired 10% of the generals and admirals across the military.

“The number crunchers say we’ve fired 10% of the generals and admirals across the force, and that number sounds about right. And I know because I directed it that we’ve also reduced the overall number of general officer slots by an additional 10%. So yes, 20% reduction across the board. Now the media calls that a purge. I call it accountability and long overdue, and frankly, the bare minimum. As usual, what the media levels as an accusation, I wear as an accomplishment,” he said during his address at Marine Base Quantico.

articles.headline: Jacob Misiorowski wraps breakout Brewers year with World Series title and a reminder that best is yet to come
keyFacts: Pitcher Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings with two hits allowed to help the Brewers win Game 5 of the World Series.
Misiorowski finished his sophomore season leading the majors in ERA, strikeouts, WHIP, and strikeout rate.
The 24-year-old pitcher is under team control through 2031 after securing his first World Series championship.
body: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- When the Brewers took the field for Game 5 of the World Series, they did so with their ace on regular rest. All that stood between them and their first World Series championship was a win with the best possible formula that they could draw up on the lineup card.

If there was any question, it was if Misiorowski could channel some of his early season magic. In the playoffs, he hadn't been bad, but hadn't been nearly as dominant as in the regular season. He also hadn't gone more than five innings in a start.

He stepped up, as championship-caliber athletes do. He was forced to leave the game late in the sixth inning due to calf cramp, but the Brewers already had a 4-0 lead (the eventual final score) and handed things off to their elite bullpen on cruise control. Misiorowski came through with 5 ⅔ innings of scoreless ball, allowing only two hits. He stifled the Rays until the game felt like it was elementary. Only two pitchers have ever recorded a scoreless start of 5+ innings with two or fewer hits allowed in a potential World Series clincher: Misiorowski and some guy named Tom Glavine in 1995.
And behind their ace, the inevitable Brewers are .

"It's awesome," Misiorowski said on the field after the Brewers clinched. "It's awesome for this team, it's awesome for the city of Milwaukee. I just made it work. It didn't matter how we won tonight, just that we won."

There were questions in the aftermath of Game 4 about whether Brewers manager Pat Murphy should have brought Misiorowski in for the bottom of the 12th to close things out. There shouldn't have been. It wasn't Game 7. The Brewers were up 3-0 in the series. Losing Game 4 meant they had full-strength Misiorowski waiting to close the door in Game 5. Unsurprisingly, he did exactly that, despite likely being on fumes from his 2026 workload.

In 2025, Misiorowski only worked 141 ⅓ innings between the minors, majors and playoffs. That was a career high in his professional career. In 2026, he finishes with 193 ⅔. It's a monster leap, and it's why the Brewers held his workloads in check down the stretch. They needed something left in the tank to achieve the ultimate goal. That was the plan all along: for him to do exactly what he did in Game 5.

And we're only scratching the proverbial surface here. Remember what a phenom Misiorowski was in the regular season, especially early in the year? He was the must-see player in the sport. Even with his workload monitored, he finished the season with a ridiculous 1.80 ERA (leading the majors) and 252 strikeouts (again, leading the majors) in 174 ⅔ innings. He also led the majors in WHIP, strikeout rate and had the lowest hit rate.

Between his rookie season and this year, "The Miz" ratcheted up his strikeout rate, plummeted his walk rate, improved his efficiency and, early in the year before workload became a concern, worked much deeper into games. As a rookie, he was a talent to dream on. As a sophomore, he was the dream. He's already as decorated as any pitcher the Brewers have ever had (with the Brewers, that is).
Now, let's keep a few things in mind. Misiorowski is:
- 24 years old;
- Under team control through 2031;
- Already a World Series champion;
- Soon to be a Cy Young winner.

After the Brewers swept the Dodgers in the NLCS, Murphy remarked on how they don't have a bunch of Hall of Famers, an indirect shot at Los Angeles' star-studded lineup, but there's an argument that Misiorowski has a strong foundation right now (so does Jackson Chourio, by the way).

Given the improvements that Misiorowski made from Year 1 to Year 2 in the majors, there's every reason to expect that next year he'll be just as good, only he'll have built up more stamina for late in the season.

Could he go 200 innings in the regular season next year and lead the Brewers to back-to-back championships while winning a second Cy Young? I don't see why not. That would have sounded like a pipe dream to Brewers fans if we got in a time machine to the aftermath of last year's sweep at the hands of those dastardly, mega-payroll Dodgers. But, you see, Misiorowski just had a dream season. With a guy with his level of talent, the only answer is to dream bigger.

articles.headline: FADU wants to take the CPU out of AI storage by putting the file system inside the SSD, but the proof won't arrive until 2027
keyFacts: FADU unveiled the File-Semantic SSD, which moves file lookups and permission checks into firmware to reduce CPU workloads.
FADU said partner samples are not expected until Q3 2027 and the first real proof will arrive by Q1 2027.
The drive embeds NFSv3 requests inside standard NVMe commands, allowing remote clients and GPUs to access files directly.
body: - FADU's File-Semantic SSD runs path lookup, permission checks, and file-to-flash mapping in firmware instead of on the host
- NFSv3 requests ride inside standard NVMe commands, so GPUs, DPUs, and remote clients can reach files without requiring a host file system
- Its headline 460,000 ops/s result came from a PCIe 5.0 host, with PCIe 6.0 results promised by Q1 2027

South Korean controller designer FADU has shown off an SSD that understands files rather than just blocks, betting that the next bottleneck in AI storage is not raw bandwidth but the CPU time spent working out where data lives.
The File-Semantic SSD (FS-SSD), unveiled at the OCP Global Summit, moves file lookup, access checks and file-to-address translation into firmware on FADU's sixth-generation controller.

FADU's whitepaper promises GPUs, DPUs and network cards a route to their files with "no host filesystem, no block layer, and no storage-server CPU in the path." Partner samples are not expected until Q3 2027.
Not the first approach to the 'CPU problem'

FADU is no newcomer to data center flash. Its Gen5 controller sits in the SN861, which Western Digital launched and SanDisk now sells; last year, the company said it had signed controller supply deals with two of the four hyperscalers, weeks after revealing its Sierra PCIe 6.0 controller.

Its pitch here, however, isn't entirely new, with the recognition coming from a not-so-surprising front: Nvidia. Nvidia has been doing the same from the other end of the PCIe bus. GPUDirect Storage removed the CPU from the data path years ago, letting drives move data straight into GPU memory, but host software still decides what to fetch and issues every request.
Its decision to open source cuFile and shift that control path onto the GPU, with SCADA attacks adding accelerator-side overhead even as FADU attacks it from the drive end of the equation.

FADU says its own measurements show the host file system and block layer consuming about 30% of CPU cycles in a GPUDirect Storage random-read workload, a vendor figure that has not been independently reproduced. It also argues that existing bypass schemes only get the CPU out of the way by abandoning files altogether.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
How does this work?

Rather than invent a new language for its drive, FADU borrowed an old one. NFS, short for Network File System, has let computers open files stored on other machines for decades. FS-SSD tucks NFS requests, such as looking up a file by name or reading part of it, inside the standard NVMe commands that SSDs already use.

Those commands can come from inside the same server or, using a networked version of NVMe called NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF), from other machines in the data center. FADU chose NFS version 3 for three reasons: it is small, with just 21 operations; it works with any operating system; and it is stateless, meaning each request carries everything the drive needs to answer it, so the drive never has to remember who has which file open.

FADU has also merged two lookups that normally happen separately. On a regular system, the computer’s file system first works out which numbered block holds each piece of a file, and the SSD’s own internal software, called the flash translation layer, then works out where that block physically sits on the flash chips.

FS-SSD does both jobs with a single file layer based on F2FS, a Linux file system designed for flash memory, laid out to match how the chips are physically organized. One map then takes the drive straight from a file to the spot where it is stored, and that map is much smaller. A typical SSD carries about 1GB of DRAM for every terabyte of flash and fills almost all of it with its block map. FS-SSD uses the same amount, but FADU says about 95% of it is left free to keep details of frequently used files close at hand.

That layout also makes cleanup simpler. Flash memory cannot overwrite old data in place, so drives regularly move the data they still need elsewhere and wipe whole blocks clean, a chore known as garbage collection.

When F2FS runs on an ordinary computer, the file system and the SSD each do their own version of this cleanup, and the two end up multiplying each other’s work. FS-SSD runs just one, and FADU says that cuts write amplification by 63% compared with F2FS on a regular host. Lower write amplification means less wear on the flash, but the 63% figure comes from simulated tests on NVMeVirt, software from Seoul National University that imitates an SSD, rather than from a real drive.

In FADU’s own preliminary test, remote file throughput held at about 460,000 ops/s as the server was cut from 16 cores to one, while a standard Linux NFS server fell from roughly 150,000 ops/s to 40,000.

The testing has its limits, though. FADU’s Gen6 drive sat in a PCIe 5.0 host, so every sequential read result topped out near 14.1GB/s, roughly the Gen5 link limit, even as Gen6 drives such as Micron’s 9650, rated for 28GB/s reads, are already in mass production.

Both the client and server ran Intel’s Core i5-13600K desktop chip with 128GB of DDR5 and a 100Gb ConnectX-6 NIC. That processor has 14 physical cores and 20 threads, so FADU’s test likely counted threads rather than physical cores.
The world’s first file-semantic SSD is an idea that isn't entirely new

FADU calls FS-SSD the world’s first file-semantic SSD, and it may well be the first hardware demonstration of its kind, but the idea isn’t new. The DevFS research paper, presented in 2018, described a direct-access file system “embedded completely within a storage device,” though the authors tested it only as an emulated prototype.

NVM Express has standardized a key-value command set that addresses data by key rather than block address, and SK hynix has developed a key-value computational storage drive with Los Alamos National Laboratory. Unlike the key-value command set, FS-SSD has no standard behind it yet. FADU has not submitted a file-semantic command set to NVM Express or OCP Storage, so for now every client needs FADU’s own software.

FADU’s longer-term goal is a flash enclosure with nothing in front of it but a PCIe switch and a DPU (a network card with its own processors) or NIC handling NVMe-oF in hardware, with a reference design built on Xsight Labs’ 800G E1 DPU due by the end of 2027.

FADU’s model puts that at about 42% lower power and 57% lower cost per 16-drive system than a conventional storage server, though those are projections rather than measurements. DPU-fronted flash boxes already exist, such as Supermicro’s BlueField-powered JBOF, but those still run the storage software on the DPU’s Arm cores. FADU wants the drives themselves to serve the files.

FADU chief executive Nam Yi-hyun said the company will use FS-SSD as “a springboard to become a leading company in AI storage solutions,” according to The Herald Business. The bottleneck FADU is chasing is real, and building on NFSv3 rather than inventing a new protocol gives it a credible starting point.

For now, though, the evidence amounts to a Gen5 test bench, an emulated write-amplification figure, and modeled savings, with OEM and ODM talks still early. The Gen6-host results FADU expects by Q1 2027 will be the first real sign of whether the drive can do the most important part: handling the CPU’s job at full speed.
