articles.headline: Obama jabs Trump over White House ‘arts and crafts’ at campaign rally in Georgia
keyFacts: Former President Barack Obama criticized President Donald Trump at a Georgia campaign rally for focusing on home renovations and gold decor instead of pressing national issues.
Sen. Jon Ossoff and Democratic gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms also spoke at the event, accusing Trump and his allies of corruption.
The rally aimed to encourage voters to support Democratic candidates in the upcoming election.
body: Former President Barack Obama launched a searing string of attacks on President Donald Trump during a rally alongside Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-GA) and Democratic gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms while on the campaign trail outside Atlanta on Wednesday evening.

After making waves last week over comments that Trump’s ballroom and additions to the White House looked as if Saddam Hussein had designed a Cheesecake Factory, Obama doubled down and took the insults further, aided by the two Democratic candidates at a United for Georgia rally inside the Arena at Southlake in southeast Atlanta.

“He’s very focused on home renovations. Should have a show on HGTV. The guy is building a ballroom that is bigger than the White House,” Obama said. “There is gold everywhere. So much gold. … The president of the United States is spending time supergluing gold medallions to the mantle in the Oval Office. I am not making this up. He is literally doing arts and crafts while we are fighting a war.”

Obama pummeled Trump on several issues but said he was particularly taken aback by how the White House and entire federal government responded to a comment he made at a Michigan campaign rally. Rather than defend its policy choices and record, the White House chose to take issue with a meaningless part of Obama’s comments, he said.

“That was the interesting thing about how the administration responded to the speech I gave the other day. They did not dispute what I said about them being directly responsible for rising prices. They did not argue with that. They did not deny tariffs were contributing to higher costs for families. They didn’t say anything about that,” Obama told the 8,000 attendees in the arena.

“I accused this administration based on the facts that they were engaging in unprecedented levels of corruption. They didn’t say anything about that. The president wasn’t even mad about the Saddam Hussein comparison. That part didn’t bother him,” Obama said. “But he was very upset about the Cheesecake Factory.”

Obama’s message focused on how Trump’s priorities were mismatched and the outcome was negatively affecting ordinary people, whom he implored to shift away from Republican politicians in next week’s election.

“After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which this country has not seen in modern times, you get to say enough is enough,” Obama said. “We’re voting for change here in Georgia.”

Ossoff took the state to a boisterous cheer from the crowd and vowed to spend his second term focused on bringing Trump and his associates in and out of government to justice for alleged corruption during his second term if Democrats are able to achieve a majority in the House or Senate.

“Never before has so little effort been made to cover up so much corruption. And here’s the bottom line: If you’re involved in any of this, next year you’ll be raising your right hand and swearing to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth shall help you now in front of the United States Congress,” Ossoff said. “The Mar-a-Lago mafia has taken American corruption to spectacular new heights. But corruption in American politics runs a lot deeper than Donald Trump. It’s been running on corporate money, secret money, billionaire money, both sides.”

Bottoms chided her competitor, Republican billionaire Rick Jackson, as a mini version of Trump who overwhelmingly favors banning abortion, allowing for the expansion of data centers, and healthcare reforms that she said would hurt the poor.

“Slick Rick has made it clear that his number one priority will be to do whatever his big daddy Donald Trump tells him to do,” Bottoms said in her remarks. “Trump and Slick Rick are more interested in serving themselves than serving the people, but on Tuesday, we get to decide what we’re going to do about it. … President Obama has reminded us that government can be a force for good, and that progress happens when we have the courage to stand in the gap for people who need it.”

Sen. Raphael Warnock (D-GA) spoke at the beginning of the rally and noted that Jackson had spent nearly $200 million of his own fortune on his campaign for governor, prompting the crowd to erupt in a “Not for Sale!” chant.
Attendees who spoke with the Washington Examiner said Obama, Ossoff, and Bottoms hit the nail on the head by linking Trump’s misdirected priorities to issues affecting voters.

Amy Smith, a 52-year-old woman from Newnan, Georgia, said the messages from all three main speakers focused on how the White House’s priorities were not in line with the public’s greatest concerns, most notably affordability.
“Trump is focusing on things that are just like decorating the ballroom and like things that are just not important to real, everyday people,” Smith told the Washington Examiner outside the arena.
Kamel Riggins, a 23-year-old therapist who attended the rally, said Obama made his point in a “humane” way that “resonated” with those in the room.

“The current administration, they have done things that have kind of affected lots of different communities,” Riggins said. “I like the aspect of how raw but also how focused they are in trying to combat and reform all of the policies that have been enacted currently.”

Jimmy Bozeman of Atlanta cited a portion of the Bible in Romans 12 that states people should live as a sacrifice for others, and said the approach Democrats laid out during their remarks was more in line with that as opposed to how the Trump administration was “taking away” low prices for gasoline “from humanity.”
TRUMP BORDER CHIEF DEFENDS BIG BEND WALL PLANS AS COURT BATTLE DELAYS CONSTRUCTION

The gubernatorial race is the tighter of the two races. Jackson led Bottoms by barely 1 percentage point, 47.8% to 46.6%, according to the average of five surveys of Georgia voters taken last month and this month.
A RealClearPolitics average of recent polls conducted in September and October revealed Ossoff had an 8.2-percentage-point advantage over Rep. Mike Collins (R-GA), 51.2% to 43%.

articles.headline: Trump, Obama trade barbs at dueling primetime rallies days before midterm elections
keyFacts: President Trump and former President Barack Obama criticized each other at competing rallies days before the midterm elections.
Trump criticized Obama's handling of Iran and White House upkeep while campaigning for Republican candidates in Ohio.
Obama criticized Trump's decision to end the Iran nuclear deal and mocked his White House renovations during an Atlanta rally.
body: President Trump and former President Barack Obama took swipes at each other Wednesday night at competing rallies less than a week before the midterm elections.

Trump, who was stumping for Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) and gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy in the Buckeye State, went after the former president over his handling of Iran and accused him of letting the White House fall into disrepair as commander-in-chief.

“The bricks were falling. The stone was broken. The monuments were coming off. The beautiful windows were cracked,” Trump said of the state of the executive mansion when he took office last January. “It looked terrible. And I fixed it very inexpensively. I paid for it myself.”
Trump argued Obama “doesn’t understand cleanliness” or that “having asphalt going through a main entrance is not the right thing.”
“We’d like to have granite with marble. We’d like to have it look nice,” the president said.

“He said, ‘Why is he spending so much time fixing up the White House? Why is he doing that?’ You know why? Because the White House is the number one symbol of our country, and we can’t have a White House with broken windows, with broken stone that hasn’t been taken in 30 years,” the president argued.
Trump is in the final stretch of a whirlwind tour of predominantly red states with tight midterm races, hoping his rallies will help Republicans maintain control of the House and Senate.
Obama has likewise been on the stump since last week, campaigning for Democrats in Michigan, Ohio and Georgia.
“I always worry when he campaigns against me,” Trump said sarcastically.
“He got involved with Hillary Clinton … and he lost. He then got involved with Kamala [Harris] and he lost,” the president continued.
Trump said his reaction upon learning Obama will be rallying for Democrats ahead of the midterms was “that’s good.”
The president also touted having “terminated” Obama’s Iran nuclear deal, which he described as the “road to a nuclear weapon for Iran, and one of the dumbest deals I’ve ever seen in my life.”
At the same time Trump was speaking in Chillicothe, Ohio, Obama went on stage in Atlanta, where he spent a good portion of his remarks going after the 45th and 47th president.
“The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions, the most important of which was to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for,” Obama said, referring to the Iran war.
“I put in place a deal that everybody acknowledged, kept them from getting nukes,” he said of the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) Trump scrapped in his first term.
Obama, who compared Trump’s White House renovations to a Cheesecake Factory run by former Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein over the weekend, dismissed conservative criticism that the zinger was elitist.
“I am the father of two daughters. You think I could have survived their childhood without going into Cheesecake Factory … that was my jam for about a decade,” he said.
“The president wasn’t even mad about the Saddam Hussein comparison,” Obama argued. “That part didn’t bother him, but he was very upset about the Cheesecake Factory comment.”

The Trump administration “mobilized a whole of government response to that joke,” Obama marveled, noting that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had lunch and spoke to reporters at a Cheesecake Factory in Washington, DC.
Obama went on to compare the Trump administration to a reality TV show.
“I want y’all to know Michelle [Obama] has love for the Real Housewives, but we gotta keep reality TV on Bravo. Leave it to the professionals. We don’t need it in the White House,” he said.

articles.headline: Milwaukee Brewers close out Tampa Bay Rays to end 57-year wait for first World Series title
keyFacts: The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 on Wednesday to win their first World Series title in the franchise's 58-year history.
William Contreras was named the series Most Valuable Player after batting .381 with four RBIs and throwing out four would-be base stealers.
Christian Yelich and manager Pat Murphy stated that the team used past playoff experiences and relentless spirit to achieve the historic victory.
body: The Milwaukee Brewers captured their first World Series crown on Wednesday night, defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 to complete a four-games-to-one victory and end more than half a century of waiting for baseball’s biggest prize.

Rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt drove in two runs and Jacob Misiorowski pitched five and two-thirds scoreless innings as Milwaukee put the finishing touches on a charmed season that began in spring training with championship ambitions and ended with the first title in the franchise’s 58th year.

Trevor Megill was mobbed by his teammates on the mound after Richie Palacios grounded to second baseman Brice Turang, who threw to Jake Bauers for the final out before a sold-out crowd of 40,489 at Tampa Bay’s Tropicana Field.

“It’s the best feeling ever. All of our fans are here. I know the city’s waited a long, long time for this and we’re so happy to bring it home to them,” said Christian Yelich, the 2018 National League MVP and the Brewers’ longest-tenured hitter. “Can’t wait to get back there and celebrate.”

William Contreras was named Most Valuable Player of the series after batting .381/.435/.429 with four RBIs across the five games, including a run-scoring double in the clincher. The 28-year-old became the eighth catcher to win the award and the first since fellow Venezuelan Salvador Perez for the Kansas City Royals in 2015.

Contreras also helped contain Tampa Bay’s vaunted running game, throwing out four would-be base stealers, including two in the opener, while using the automated ball-strike challenge system to overturn 10 of 13 calls behind the plate. The honor capped a year in which he also won the World Baseball Classic with Venezuela.
“I don’t want to offend any of the other catchers in the league,” Contreras said. “But sitting up here today, champion of the world, I feel like I’m the best catcher in the league.”

The Brewers, who arrived in Milwaukee in 1970 after one season as the Seattle Pilots, had reached the World Series only once before, bowing to the St Louis Cardinals in seven games in 1982 as American League champions. They switched to the National League in 1998, but that narrow defeat remained the nearest they had come until this year, when a team blending young talent with October experience finally went one step further.

Milwaukee had been three outs from completing a sweep on Tuesday night in Game 4 before surrendering a 12th-inning lead. Given another opportunity on Wednesday, the Brewers built a four-run advantage behind Misiorowski, the brilliant right-hander who scattered two hits and one walk while striking out two before departing with a right calf cramp.

Tampa Bay’s best early opportunity came in the fourth, when Liam Hicks was hit by a pitch and Chandler Simpson singled, with Sal Frelick’s fielding error leaving runners at second and third with two outs. Misiorowski induced a groundout from Ben Williamson, whose pinch-hit single had won Game 4, to leave both runners stranded. He then put down the Rays in order in the fifth.

“I don’t even have words,” said Misiorowski, the overwhelming favorite to win the NL Cy Young award who broke the World Series velocity record with a 103.5mph fastball on the first pitch of Game 1 last Friday. “I know they’re going crazy in Milwaukee.” Asked about the Brewers’ fans, thousands of whom had transformed the drab domed stadium in downtown St Petersburg into a home away from home, he added: “They’ve been nothing but supportive this year and in years prior and it has been amazing.”

Pratt, who made his major league debut in June and collected four hits in Tuesday’s defeat, again supplied an important part of Milwaukee’s offense. Turang doubled in the second inning and, after Frelick was hit by a pitch, scored on Pratt’s single to center. Pratt was caught trying to reach second, but the Brewers had the lead.
“This is one of the greatest moments of my life. Oh my gosh. It doesn’t even feel real,” Pratt said afterward. “This is surreal. It only took four months!”
Tampa Bay starter Drew Rasmussen, pitching on three days’ rest, kept the deficit at one through four innings before manager Kevin Cash turned to his bullpen.

Milwaukee immediately doubled their lead. Pratt singled off Kevin Kelly, Garrett Mitchell followed with another single and David Hamilton’s ground-ball single to right brought Pratt home for a 2-0 advantage.

The Brewers widened the gap in the sixth. Yelich was hit by a Garrett Cleavinger pitch and scored on Contreras’s double to left. Turang singled, then stole second after Tyler Wells entered. Following a Frelick strikeout, Pratt lifted a sacrifice fly into foul territory in right, scoring Contreras to make it 4-0.

The Rays threatened in the ninth. Hicks doubled with one out and, after Jonny DeLuca struck out, Simpson lined an RBI double to right off Megill, cutting Milwaukee’s lead to 4-1 and bringing the potential tying run into the on-deck circle. But Megill stranded Simpson at second to end Tampa Bay’s campaign.

The championship capped a season in which Milwaukee posted a major league-best 103-59 record before winning the NL pennant for the first time with a sweep of the deep-pocketed Dodgers in the NLCS. The Brewers switched over from the American League in 1998 as part of the realignment accompanying the arrival of the expansion Rays and Arizona Diamondbacks.

For Pat Murphy, it was the crowning achievement of his third season managing the Brewers. The 67-year-old, previously Craig Counsell’s bench coach, had already won consecutive NL manager of the year awards before helming Milwaukee to the promised land.

“The years of getting eliminated or being beaten last year by the Dodgers, that was a blessing because we learned from it and we grew, and we came in with a different attitude,” Murphy said. “We came in with a spirit about us, and we weren’t going to be denied.”
“We weren’t great at a lot of things, but we were relentless,” he added.

The Brewers established their total command of the matchup with three consecutive victories: a narrow win in the opener, a comeback from four runs down in Game 2 and a 10-1 rout in Game 3. Tuesday’s setback denied them the chance to become the first team since the 1976 Cincinnati Reds to sweep both the league championship series and World Series, but merely postponed the inevitable.
Tampa Bay, who won an American League-best 98 games, were left with a third World Series defeat following losses in 2008 and 2020.

“Tonight we ran into a team that had elite starting pitching, very good pitching, and then as elite of a bullpen as I’ve ever seen,” Tampa Bay manager Kevin Cash said. Milwaukee’s relievers finished the postseason with a 1.38 ERA, the fourth-lowest in history among teams with at least 40 relief innings.

The Brewers’ triumph marked the city of Milwaukee’s first World Series championship since 1957, when Lew Burdette’s three complete-game victories powered the Braves past the New York Yankees in a seven-game classic, delivering the city’s first professional sports title. The Braves relocated to Atlanta nine years later.

This year’s Fall Classic guaranteed a first-time champion for only the second time in 107 years and the first since Philadelphia faced Kansas City in 1980. Milwaukee claimed that distinction, leaving the Rays, Colorado Rockies, San Diego Padres and Seattle Mariners as the four active major league franchises still seeking their first title.

Amid the celebrations, Yelich remembered the beloved Brewers broadcaster Bob Uecker, who died last year aged 90. “He’s smiling, man. He’s smiling. I really wish he could have been here to see this,” he said. “This one’s still for Bob and this is still for you.”

articles.headline: Anduril now says its BlueChip laptop will meet Buy American standards at launch
keyFacts: Defense contractor Anduril and chipmaker Qualcomm announced a partnership to build laptops entirely in the United States starting in 2027.
Anduril communications VP Shannon Prior stated that the BlueChip laptop will meet the 65 percent U.S. domestic-content threshold at launch.
Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon stated that the laptop's processors will be manufactured at a TSMC facility in Arizona.
body: On Tuesday, defense contractor Anduril and chipmaker Qualcomm announced a partnership to build laptops entirely in the United States, starting with a single model in 2027. They also announced a “long-term goal” of pushing the computer industry to create “a fully domestic supply chain.”
Anduril now says its BlueChip laptop will meet Buy American standards at launch
Palmer Luckey says it was always the goal, and now the company is committing to it.

Even a single Made-in-USA laptop would be a surprise, because no major US computer company builds its laptops here — not Apple, not Dell, not HP, not Microsoft. We’re not aware of any company that does.

But we are aware of companies that have briefly and strategically assembled computers here seemingly to appease President Donald Trump. We’re also aware of companies that have promised US jobs only to deliver empty buildings. And we’re aware of at least one fake “US” company that lied to the government about making product domestically.

That’s why we now ask pointed questions when a company says it’s committed to US manufacturing. We asked TP-Link those sorts of questions just over a week ago. On Monday, we asked Anduril founder Palmer Luckey and Qualcomm president and CEO Cristiano Amon those kinds of questions.
Over the course of two days, Anduril has changed its answers.

Anduril communications VP Shannon Prior now says the company’s laptop will have at least 65 percent of its components made in the US by the time it launches in 2027. It’s an important number, and one that Anduril did not commit to earlier this week.

Luckey held a call with reporters on Monday, during which he was clear that he wants to make literally every part of a computer in the United States — and that Anduril and Qualcomm have already mapped out a plan. “We have a technical roadmap to get to 100 percent domestic over time,” he told journalists.

Luckey also suggested his laptop would be built to comply with the requirements of the military and other government agencies — and that it would meet or exceed one specific US government standard that has an exact definition.
“We are not just barely meeting the bar for Made in America. We are going hard to make this an all-American play, and not even the Buy American Act requires what we’re trying,” Luckey said.

The Buy American Act dates back to 1933, but it was updated during the Biden Administration to require that at least 65 percent of the cost of a company’s products must be made domestically for it be considered a domestic product itself. That number is going up to 75 percent in 2029.

Many products need to be made in America to those standards, or federal agencies can’t buy them without receiving a waiver — which agencies currently use en masse, Luckey himself argued on the call. “There’s a number of government agencies that are required by law to buy American-made computers [...] All of those procurements are happening under waivers of those laws,” he said.

We also noticed that Anduril’s press release specifies that its first laptop will be “designed and assembled” in the United States, not necessarily “manufactured” here (though the release does talk about future manufacturing). This was also a sticking point with router maker TP-Link, which would not confirm full manufacturing even after suggesting it in an interview with The Verge.
That’s why we asked Luckey what percent of his first laptop’s components would be made in the US. His reply was not 65 percent or 70 percent. It was “TBD.” You can read the exchange for yourself:
The Verge: When it arrives in 2027, what percent of the components in the BlueChip laptop will be made in the US?

Luckey: TBD. I’m doing my very, very best. It’s gonna be a whole mix of things based on when do certain memory fabs come online? When do certain CPU, GPU fabs come online? There’s a whole— Like, am I able to get a display line here or not? Do I have to do that after launch? I’m being totally open kimono with you here. Those questions are not settled. It is not clear if I will be able. I know the glass is gonna be made in the US, I know the frame is gonna be made in the US around that display. I know that parts of the ribbon component are gonna be made in the U.S. I don’t know if I will have successfully pulled that component in or a dozen other components. So it’s a little up in the air. I’m doing my very, very best. I think most likely the thing that we ship is not going to be 100-percent American. I think it’ll be a blend of US and allies around the world, mostly US, probably a few things from some allies, and then that’ll be in the context of conversations with those allies about bringing those components into production in the United States, and I’m being honest with the government on this too. I mean, I’ve had conversations where I’ve said, listen. I would love to give you guys an American, 100-percent American laptop right off the bat, but that is not the environment the US government has created or US industry has created. I can’t let the perfect be the enemy of the good.

When we followed up by email to ask specifically about 65 percent, the answer was that the laptop prototype is currently at 32 percent and Anduril could not yet commit to 65 percent. Here’s Anduril spokesperson Stephanie Davis’ full reply on Tuesday:
For the prototype today, approximately 32% is U.S.-origin by component procurement cost, and more than 90% is sourced from the United States and allied countries combined.

We’re working to expand domestic sourcing and production ahead of planned availability in 2027, with the goal of eliminating foreign content and ultimately establishing an end-to-end American supply chain.

The final domestic-content percentage at launch remains unsettled, so we can’t confirm above or below 65% today. That’s why we’re asking you to revise the assertion that it will be “well below” that threshold.
Today, Prior writes that Anduril can indeed commit to 65 percent. Here is the most recent statement:

Our previous response to The Verge was incorrect. The BlueChip laptop is indeed being developed to exceed the 65% U.S. domestic-content threshold at launch in 2027. Meeting that threshold is a fundamental objective of the program. The precise domestic-content percentage of the final product is still being determined as we finalize suppliers and work through prototypes, and we look forward to sharing more next year.

Today’s statement is the first time Anduril has confirmed that we, and government agencies, theoretically shouldn’t need to wait until Anduril achieves its full goals to see a laptop that meets the Buy American standard. If everything works out, Anduril’s first laptop in 2027, with Qualcomm, should be that laptop.

We invited Luckey to explain how Anduril would get to 65 percent domestic component production in a follow-up interview, but we were told he’s not currently available. On the Monday call, he told journalists that Anduril already has a US glassmaker lined up for the laptop’s cover glass, is programming FPGAs (field-programmable gate arrays) to serve the purpose of power management chips and other circuits it can’t normally can’t get outside China, and is developing made-in-America batteries as well.
The press release adds that the enclosure is designed “for US machining” and the laptop will use metals “that US industry can produce and machine at scale.”

As for the laptop’s Snapdragon processor, we asked Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon about that. “TSMC has a manufacturing facility in Arizona, and that’s where our chips are going to be made,” he told The Verge.

articles.headline: ‘They mobilized a whole government response to that joke’: Obama laughs off Trump attacks in rally for Ossoff
keyFacts: Barack Obama campaigned near Atlanta on Wednesday to support Georgia Democrats in the final week of the midterm election campaign.
The rally supported Jon Ossoff and Keisha Lance Bottoms, who is statistically tied in polls for the Georgia governor's race.
Democrats have pledged to impeach Donald Trump if they take control of Congress next year, according to Jon Ossoff.
body: Barack Obama, speaking at a Wednesday campaign rally in suburban Atlanta, offered a closing argument for Democrats in the final week of the midterm election campaign.
“These are not serious people,” he said of Donald Trump and the Republican party. “And we’re all paying the price for their lack of seriousness.”

Obama came to Georgia to support the campaigns of US senator Jon Ossoff, former Atlanta mayor and gubernatorial hopeful Keisha Lance Bottoms, and an array of down-ballot Democrats as part of his cross-country campaign tour before next week’s election. From 3,500 to 4,000 people filled the Discovery Center of Clayton county for the late election season stop, just south of Atlanta.

Obama has been casting caltrops behind him with each campaign stop, offering pointed criticism of Republican candidates and Donald Trump that has been unusual for the former president. He continued to do so on Wednesday, again invoking the image of Trump’s gilded renovations of the White House and noting Trump’s strident reaction to his crack last week likening it to Saddam Hussein decorating a Cheesecake Factory.

“The Saddam Hussein thing didn’t bother him. But he was very upset about the Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said. “I mean, it’s all crazy, but this is the crazy part: they mobilized a whole government response to that joke.

“The White House even called the secretary of the treasury,” the former president continued. “The guy who is trying to figure out how to lower inflation … they told him he should hold a press conference in front of the Cheesecake Factory.”
He also rebuffed Republicans’ accusations of snobbery for referencing the popular chain restaurant.
“I am the father of two daughters,” Obama said. “Do you think I could have survived their childhood without going to the Cheesecake Factory?”
But he turned that discussion to the problems of affordability for American voters, in contrast with the corruption of the presidency.
“We have never seen a president so intent on selling favors,” Obama said. “The guy has made billions of dollars while in office. Understand that this has not been done in modern times.”
The construction of a new ballroom on the site of the former East Wing of the White House featured in the comments of many speakers at Wednesday’s rally, including Ossoff.
“Each day, Donald Trump digs the moral pit deeper,” Ossoff said, accusing the president of leading “the most corrupt administration of all time, and everybody knows it”.

“If you’re involved in any of this, next year you’ll be raising your hand to tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth,” Ossoff said, in reference to Democrats pledging to impeach Trump if they take control of Congress next year.
The crowd chanted: “Lock him up!” in response.

Bottoms, meanwhile, contrasted her candidacy with that of her Republican opponent Rick Jackson, tying the billionaire healthcare executive to Trump and describing them as “two out-of-touch billionaires who want to keep getting rich on the backs of taxpayers”.

Invoking the legacies of US Representative John Lewis and Coretta Scott King, Bottoms characterized her candidacy as transcending politics. “They may have the money, but they will never overtake our movement,” she said.

Despite a broad wave of Democratic support buoying candidates across the country – and the eight- to 10-point polling lead Ossoff has on his Republican opponent, US Representative Mike Collins – Bottoms is statistically tied in polls with Jackson. If elected, Bottoms would break the state’s Republican trifecta – where the GOP has controlled both chambers of the legislature and the governor’s office – which began in 2004.
Rev Raphael Warnock, Georgia’s other senator, warned of “spiritual wickedness in high places” while describing the effects of deep cuts to Medicaid and Snap nutrition support for children.

“This is about the character of the country,” Warnock said. “This is about who we are and whether we are here for one another … I am concerned about the spiritual health of our country. There is brokenness, because only a broken nation could manage to elect Donald Trump twice.”

Trump, who was campaigning in Ohio at the same time as the Georgia rally, has also been on a national rally blitz, holding near-daily events in the final days of the midterm campaign. Trump has made two appearances in as many weeks in Georgia, both in what would otherwise seem to be congressional districts that are safe territory for Republicans.

articles.headline: Qatari mediators hand Iran new proposal to end the war
keyFacts: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Iran continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed regarding peace proposals.
The Saudi-led coalition announced it intercepted a ballistic missile fired by Houthi forces toward Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province.

body: What to know about the Iran war today:

- Iran's foreign minister said Wednesday the country "continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed" after Reuters earlier reported Tehran rejected Qatar's latest peace proposal, saying they had come with "unacceptable" ideas.

- Israelis voted Tuesday in a national, with the looming large. Exit polls projected that a majority of Israelis voted against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition but neither side had a clear margin of victory.
- The has cost the U.S. military at least $47.1 billion as of mid-October, according to a new estimate from U.S. Central Command obtained by CBS News.
Saudi Arabia intercepts ballistic missile fired by Houthis, officials say
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday it had intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the group at the kingdom's eastern region.
"Air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Eastern Province," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki posted on X.
Saudi Arabia has this month come under sustained attack from the Iran-backed Houthis, including a strike on Riyadh's international airport that was the kingdom's deadliest in years.
The Houthis said this week they had targeted the Ras Tanura refinery in the oil-rich Eastern Province with a ballistic missile.
Tehran has denied having anything to do with attacks by the Houthis after Saudi Arabia accused Iran of having encouraged the group's escalation against the kingdom.
Following an uneasy four-year truce, fighting reignited in Yemen in July, months into the U.S.-Iran conflict that has plunged the wider region into crisis.
Hezbollah says it doesn't care who wins Israeli election
Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem said Wednesday the Iran-backed Lebanese movement was not concerned with , vowing to continue its "resistance" against the neighbouring country no matter who wins.

With 85% of ballots counted, the right-wing bloc of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had a slight lead over the main opposition bloc, led by Gadi Eisenkot, but was still short of a majority after Tuesday's election.
"We do not concern ourselves with who governs Israel, but let it be perfectly clear that it cannot continue its occupation and must leave our land," Qassem said in a written statement.

"The resistance will continue ... and will stand up to the aggression directed against it and against Lebanon, and there is no room to discuss the disarmament" of Hezbollah "as long as the occupation persists and its aggression continues," he added.
The group, which once dominated political life in Lebanon, has been weakened by the two wars it has waged against Israel since 2023.
U.K. seeks to give households "breathing space" this winter over Iran war energy price spike
U.K. Treasury chief John Healey used his first budget Wednesday to offer households and businesses some support with energy bills this winter in the face of what he termed "global economic storms."
He said that his "choice in the budget today is to give families and businesses some breathing space now," as the consequences of the Middle East conflict play out.

"For families, that means higher prices at the pump, higher energy bills and higher mortgages," he said in his statement, one of the main dates of the parliamentary calendar. "For businesses, higher running costs and more expensive loans. And the impact is felt in the public finances, too."

Among the measures announced was a 100-pound ($133) one-off payment this winter for 20 million lower- and middle-income households, proportionately more of whom live in the electoral battlegrounds in northern England.
Other measures include the extension of a cut in the sales tax on electricity bills and the abolition of a charge paid on gas bills.
Netanyahu accuses Arab parties of stealing election, widespread fraud
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused the Arab parties of stealing the election through widespread fraud and called on Shin Bet, Israel's security agency, to investigate.

"We demand from the police and the Shin Bet a thorough investigation into the election theft by the Arab parties and the full prosecution of the criminals," Netanyahu's Likud party shared on his X account, translated from Hebrew. "This is a serious blow to Israeli democracy and the voting rights of Israeli citizens. The law enforcement agencies must act with an iron fist and in an immediate manner."

Netanyahu's party , but all of the parties will fall short of the majority needed to control the Knesset, Israel's parliament. With 85% of votes counted, Netanyahu's Likud party has 20.8% and Eisenkot's Yashar party has 16.1%, according to official election data.

Local media projected 53 seats for the Likud party, 48 seats for the Yahar and other opposition parties and 19 seats for the Arab-led parties. In order to reach a majority (61 of 120 seats) and pick a prime minister, deals will have to be made.
Iran continues to review ideas for peace agreement, foreign minister says

Amid reports Iran had rejected the latest proposal for peace from Qatari intermediaries, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi posted on X that his country continues to review ideas for a diplomatic solution to the eight-month war.

"While our Brave Armed Forces are fully prepared to defend the Homeland, Iran continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed," Araghchi wrote. "We remain in close and ongoing contact with intermediaries to review ideas that can ensure implementation of our 7-Day Plan in even less than a week."

The seven-day plan was presented to the U.S. shortly after the U.N. General Assembly in September. However, President Trump rejected the idea presented by Iran for a seven-day ceasefire and then phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
Earlier Wednesday, a senior Iranian official denied Qatar had presented Tehran with a new peace proposal on Sunday, saying instead Qatar had only come with "unacceptable" ideas, Reuters reported.
A source had earlier reported there were concerns Israel could begin a new bombing campaign after its election, according to Reuters.
Kuwait summons Iran ambassador over "interference"
Kuwait summoned Iran's envoy in protest on Wednesday, after Tehran denied one of its citizens, sentenced to death in Kuwait, was involved in an assassination plot targeting a top government figure.

Earlier this week, two Kuwaiti judicial sources told the AFP news agency that the Gulf state had condemned three Shia men to death for plotting the assassination of Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Fahad al-Yousef, collaborating with Iran; and for membership in Hezbollah.

Iran's embassy in Kuwait said earlier Wednesday it "rejects the Kuwaiti government's claim regarding the involvement of an Iranian citizen in a plot to assassinate figures or in any other act that could harm Kuwaiti national security."
It added that the person in question had been outside Kuwait for 10 years.
It said it regretted a "negative approach towards Iran, manifested, among other things, in the repetition of flimsy and worn-out scenarios concerning Iranian interference in Kuwaiti affairs."

In response, Kuwait summoned Iranian ambassador Mohammad Toutounji over the statement, which it said "constituted blatant interference in the internal affairs of the State of Kuwait and an infringement upon its sovereignty and the independence of its judiciary."
Abdulredha Haydar Dahqani was among those who had been sentenced to death, the judicial sources told AFP.
Dahqani, an Iranian national, had already been handed the death penalty in 2016 after he was tried in absentia along with 25 Kuwaitis. He was convicted of spying for Iran and plotting attacks.
Another was Hussein Abdallah al-Maatouq, a religious dignitary and secretary-general of the National Islamic Alliance, Kuwait's most influential Shia movement, the sources said.
CBS/AFP
Israeli defense minister slams Eisenkot's call for military to resist Netanyahu's pressure

Israel's defense minister on Wednesday denounced opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot for urging the military to resist post-election pressure from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has threatened new strikes on Iran.

"His call to senior military officials not to obey the directives of the prime minister or me or of other relevant security authorities, on the grounds that 'they have his support,' is an anti-democratic statement detached from reality," Israel Katz wrote on X.

Eisenkot, a former military chief, said in a speech to supporters after Tuesday's election that Netanyahu was a caretaker prime minister lacking a mandate and the military should serve the state rather than the premier.
"Stand firm in the face of any attempt to challenge you. You have my unequivocal backing. Netanyahu, do not dare use Israel's security for your political needs," Eisenkot said.
Netanyahu has repeatedly threatened in recent days to renew strikes on Iran.
Media reports, denied by Netanyahu, said military chief Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir pushed back immediately before the election on the prime minister's new plans on Iran.
Eisenkot's comments were the latest in "a campaign of lies" about tension between Netanyahu and the military over Iran, Katz said.
Yemen's transport ministry warns of civil aviation risks after sixth Houthi attack on Aden airport

Yemen's Ministry of Transport has warned of risks to civil aviation safety after Aden International Airport was targeted in a missile attack attributed to the Houthi group for the sixth time, Saudi Arabia's Asharq News reported.
The missile strike shook parts of the southern city, raising fresh concerns over the safety of airport operations and the potential threat to civilian air traffic.
Airport authorities had evacuated all employees and workers from the facility following Houthi threats to target the airport.
Iran, Russia near agreement on joint development of small modular nuclear reactors

Iran is finalizing a protocol with Russia to accelerate joint development of small modular nuclear reactors, Behrouz Kamalvandi, spokesman and deputy for international, legal and parliamentary affairs at the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran, has announced.

Speaking to Iran's Shabakeh Khabar television network, Kamalvandi said the agreement would facilitate closer cooperation on the construction of small modular reactors, a technology attracting growing international interest as countries seek reliable, low-carbon electricity sources. SMRs are far smaller than traditional large-scale reactors.

Kamalvandi also highlighted rising global electricity demand, driven in part by artificial intelligence, digital technologies and the electrification of transport. He said nuclear power could provide stable baseload electricity while helping reduce emissions.

He claimed Iran's nuclear industry had reached a mature stage and said the country had developed substantial domestic capabilities in nuclear plant construction, fuel-cycle technology and nuclear safety. He also stated political pressure had delayed some Iranian projects but had not halted the country's nuclear activities.

Kamalvandi made the remarks while discussing Iran's participation in an international ministerial conference on nuclear energy in South Korea. He said the Iranian delegation was using the event to promote international cooperation and argue that countries party to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty should have their rights respected alongside their obligations.
Iran warns any Israeli-led attack would be "devastating" for global markets
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned on Wednesday that any Israeli-instigated attack in the Gulf region would have a "devastating impact" on global markets.
"Devastating impact on int'l markets of any Israel-instigated military misadventure in Persian Gulf region remains major concern for both gas suppliers and consumers," Araghchi said in a post on X.
The United States and Israel have in recent days raised the prospect of renewed attacks on Iran in the war, which began in late February with strikes on the Islamic republic.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is seeking to form a new government after close elections, said on Wednesday he could work with President Trump to eliminate the "existential threat" posed by Iran.
CBS/AFP
Iranian embassy in Kuwait denies assassination plot allegations against Iranian citizen

Iran's Embassy in Kuwait has categorically rejected the Kuwaiti government's allegation that an Iranian citizen was involved in a or in any other activity that could undermine Kuwait's national security.

The embassy said in a statement that it "categorically rejects the allegation made by the Kuwaiti government regarding the involvement of an Iranian citizen in a plot to assassinate public figures or in any other act that could undermine Kuwait's national security, and recalls that the aforementioned individual has not been present in Kuwait at any time during the past ten years."

A Kuwaiti State Security and Terrorism Criminal Court sentenced three men to death on Monday over an alleged plot to assassinate First Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Al-Yousef, with prosecutors accusing the defendants of spying for Iran, communicating with Iranian-linked entities and joining Hezbollah, two judicial sources told the AFP news agency Tuesday.
The court also sentenced eight other defendants to varying prison terms.

According to Kuwaiti newspaper Al-Rai, the defendants were accused of communicating with Iran and entities allegedly operating in its interests, including Lebanese group Hezbollah, to carry out hostile acts against Kuwait following the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei on Feb. 28, at the beginning of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.
Saudi strike kills 14, Houthis say, as group targets Aden
Iran-backed Houthi rebels said Wednesday Saudi Arabia killed dozens of people with strikes in Yemen. The group also said it had targeted the perimeter of an airport in government-held Aden

Houthi broadcaster Almasirah reported 14 dead "and 10 wounded, including women and children in a preliminary toll," in attacks blamed on Saudi Arabia that hit a market and a petrol station in the northwestern Jawf province.
In Aden, a Houthi missile fell inside the perimeter of the airport shortly before the Iran-backed group issued a call to evacuate the area, a local police source told the AFP news agency.
The source added that the strike hit while a Saudi military aircraft was at the airport, but the plane "was not hit and took off shortly afterward."
He spoke on condition of anonymity due to security concerns.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a post on Telegram that the cargo plan was "transporting weapons to kill the sons of the Yemeni people."
The Houthis have targeted Aden several times in recent weeks. They have also intensified attacks on their Saudi foe, while they battle the government it backs in Aden.
CBS/AFP
U.S. reportedly warns Gulf allies to prepare for brief, intense campaign against Iran post-midterms
The United States has told its Gulf allies to prepare for a brief but intense campaign against Iran after the midterm elections, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people briefed on the matter.

The U.S. military is shipping a Patriot antimissile system from Texas to Israel and has transferred troops off bases where they may have been vulnerable, officials familiar with the decisions told the outlet.

American forces across the Middle East have been restocking munitions and aircraft have been preparing for strikes, the paper reported, while an additional aircraft carrier strike group and Marine unit are set to join the 20 or so warships in the region, though some other vessels could be withdrawn.
Houthis call for immediate evacuation of Yemen's Aden airport

The Houthis have called on people in Aden International Airport in southern Yemen to evacuate immediately, claiming that a Saudi military cargo aircraft is transporting weapons there intended to kill Yemenis.

Houthi military spokesperson Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said in a post on X: "Our armed forces call on those present at Aden Airport to evacuate the airport immediately, due to the presence of an enemy Saudi military cargo aircraft transporting weapons to kill the sons of the Yemeni people."
Aden is the seat of the Saudi-backed Yemeni government, and has been since the Iran-backed Houthis took the country's capital, Sanaa, in 2014.
Senior Iranian official denies Qatar presented new peace proposal, says ideas "unacceptable"
A senior Iranian official denied Wednesday that Qatar had presented Tehran with a new peace proposal, saying instead that Qatar had come with "unacceptable" ideas, the Reuters news agency reported.
Reuters reported earlier Wednesday that Qatari mediators handed Iran a new draft deal to end the war on Sunday, citing an official briefed on the negotiations.
Dismissing the idea that they had been given a new peace proposal, the Iranian official speaking to the news agency said Tehran would show no flexibility on the nuclear issue.
Qatari mediators hand Iran new proposal to end the war, Reuters reports
Qatari mediators on Sunday handed Iran a new draft deal to end the war, the Reuters news agency reported, citing an official briefed on the negotiations.
Tehran is considering the proposal and set to respond by the end of the week, the agency reported Wednesday.
The source added that there were concerns in Tehran before the meeting on Sunday that Israel could resume its bombardment of Iran this week.
Cost of Iran war rises to an estimated $47 billion
The cost of the Iran war has risen to an estimated $47 billion, according to an estimate from the U.S. military's Central Command obtained by CBS News Tuesday.
Like previous estimates, it does not include damage to U.S. military bases in the Middle East. The bulk of the cost, $29 billion, is for replacing expended munitions.
According to a by the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office in September, the Iran war could cost approximately $2 billion to $3 billion per month for as long as it continues.
Israeli election exit polls show race headed toward stalemate

Exit polls from Israel's major television networks project that a majority of Israelis voted against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition in Tuesday's election, but his Likud party still emerged as the largest party among all the contenders. Neither bloc, Netanyahu or the opposition, has a clear majority.
While Netanyahu appears to have won fewer votes than his main challenger, according to the early exit polls, both candidates will likely struggle to cobble together a coalition.
One or the other would need to obtain majority support in Israel's 120-seat parliament, known as the Knesset, in order to form a government.

Israel's two Arab parties won more seats in parliament than in any previous election. That electoral success comes after what some Arab voters told CBS News was a difficult time for them in the country under the hard-right government of Netanyahu, prompting a historic turnout for the minority community.

Both Netanyahu and those opposing him have vowed not to form a government reliant on Arab parties, arguing it would endanger the country if they gain enough seats to influence Israel's engagement in its myriad conflicts. Arab citizens of Israel are around 20% of the population.

articles.headline: I've spent over 50 hours in Phantom Blade Zero—here are my top 20 tips to conquer the Wulin
keyFacts: PC Gamer published twenty gameplay tips for Phantom Blade Zero, detailing how the martial arts action game diverges from typical soulslikes.
The article reported that players do not lose souls upon death and resting at bells does not cause enemies to respawn.
Recommendations for players include exploring thoroughly, attacking constantly with regular moves, and utilizing specific combat counters and weapons.
body: Phantom Blade Zero is a masterful martial arts action game, but even those who played Black Myth Wukong will likely be surprised by how much it diverges from typical soulslikes or even Sekiro's structure. You don't lose Remnant Echoes (souls) when you die, and enemies don't respawn when you rest, to name just a couple of big departures.

It's not a particularly tough game unless you play on max difficulty, and if, like me, you complete all the side content, you'll likely find yourself steamrolling in the late game. Still, for fans of souls and Sekiro-style action games, it'll take a little adjustment to work out how to approach Phantom Blade Zero differently.
1. Explore thoroughly
Attack power, Sha-Chi (stamina) and HP are increased by collectibles you find or get by defeating enemy encounters. Specifically: Blackstone, Sha-Chi Amber, and Memory Flowers.
2. Examine everything
Investigating objects or notes rewards Remnant Dust (souls) in Phantom Blade Zero, but can also reveal new sidequests.
3. Attack constantly
Your regular attacks (X on controller) don't consume stamina, but they will deal damage and chip down a boss's Sha-Chi, so be aggressive.
4. Collect Memory Flowers

Besides granting HP and story fragments, collecting all Memory Flowers before a region boss often gives them an extra phase or sometimes a unique reward, such as a weapon. You'll be introduced to these in the Crimson Forest.
5. Remember red is right, blue is left
When an attack flashes red, hit the right bumper on controller. When it flashes blue, hit the left. Or if you're struggling to react or remember, just hit both.
6. Dodge smoky black attacks also
You'll first experience these stamina-draining attacks fighting Peng Meng, where the boss emits a smoky black aura. Dodge these instead of blocking to retain your Sha-Chi.
7. Use Sha-Chi combos to deal damage

Your Sha-Chi combos (Y on controller) cost stamina, but deal more damage—use these after you parry a red or blue attack, or when you've broken your opponent's Sha-Chi, meaning they can't block for a while.
8. Experiment with weapons
You can refund all materials and Remnant Dust from an upgraded weapon or Phantom Edge. It's free up to Level 10. After that it costs a reforge talisman, which are easy to find.
9. Pay attention to your skills
Every five upgrade levels a weapon or Phantom Edge gain a new ability, either passive or active—make sure to learn what these are to use them in combat.
10. Use your Phantom Edges

Unlike Sekiro, where Shinobi tools cost a limited talisman resource, you get a fixed amount of sparks (Phantom Edge uses) every time you rest, plus you can recoup them using certain skills and accessories.
11. Rest at bells often
Resting at bells in Phantom Blade Zero doesn't reset enemies as in soulslikes, but it will replenish your medicine healing items and spark uses for Phantom Edges.
12. Counter for free
When you see an RT (on controller) appear on an enemy, it means you can use your equipped Phantom Edge without it costing a spark, so make sure to take advantage of this.
13. Use weapons of different types

I'd suggest a one-handed and two-handed weapon. Different weapons have different strengths, but each type uses a separate upgrade material. Some weapons, like Jagged Steel, deal statuses which are only effective against some enemies.
14. Polish your accessories
Accessories are very strong, especially as you unlock more slots and the ability to buff their effect when you arrive in the Village of Lu. Besides weapons, this is where your build comes from.
15. You can die lots
Unlike soulslikes, you don't lose Remnant Echoes when you die in Phantom Blade Zero and even if you die to a boss during its second phase, you'll start the fight from that same phase.
16. Don't forget about stealth
It's introduced in the early game, but it's easy to forget you can go stealth anytime. Assassinations, in particular, are very strong, as you can often follow up to assassinate a second enemy nearby.
17. Upgrade your medicine
18. Complete Banyan Trees
19. Some quests are missable

If you have a quest with tracking markers located in your current region that you can reach or access, it's a good idea to finish it before you leave. Some quests can fail, though there are plenty where you're expected to return later also.
20. Come back later

If you're struggling with an optional boss, such as the Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet or Gold-Masked One, remember you can come back later. Phantom Blade Zero doesn't have many points of no return, so you have plenty of time to get stronger.

articles.headline: Details of thousands of US immigration agents leaked in major hack
keyFacts: Personal details of more than 41000 US Department of Homeland Security personnel were leaked online by groups including the Department of Peace.
A DHS spokesperson said the agency is aware of the breach and is actively working to address the situation.
The leaked database included names and work contact information for employees across multiple agencies including Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
body: - Published
Details of more than 41,000 personnel working for the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including thousands involved in immigration enforcement, have been leaked to the public.

The leak includes names, work addresses and phone numbers of DHS staff, including agents working with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection, along with descriptions of the work they do for each agency.
Wednesday's leak marks the third time in recent weeks that a government agency has been targeted by leaks or hacks.
A DHS spokesperson said the agency is "aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively."
"We take all security threats against our employees and officers seriously and will work to ensure all are properly protected," the spokesperson added.
"We will update the public when more information is available."

The seemingly unprecedented breach of employee information was made public online. A group called the Department of Peace accessed the information from DHS, while journalist and cybersecurity researcher maia crimew alongside the website Distributed Denial of Secrets put it online.
The information was put in a database named Icepick.
Most of the agents included, more than 21,000 of them, work for CBP, according to the data. Nearly 6,600 work for ICE.
Other records show agents with Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Protective Service and even people working for the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.

The leaked information also included dozens of previously unknown operation names, the agents that led and worked on those operations, and some of the technology they used in their work, including tech provided by Cellbrite and Palantir.

The groups wrote in an online statement that the the leak was not meant to be a directory of every DHS agent. Rather the aim was to replace "anonymity with accountability", according to Emma Best, a co founder of DDoSecrets.

"The leak is extraordinary but deceptive in it's simplicity as it identifies the officials responsible for overseeing covert and undercover operations, the government's hunt for leakers and the failed BlueLeaks investigation - along with key personnel in DHS's ever-escalating rendition and deportation programs," Best added.
BlueLeaks refers to a massive leak of US police data in 2020, data from which DDoSecrets also hosted.
A spokesperson for the Department of Peace pointed directly at actions by ICE agents for the groups work to hack DHS records.
"On July 17th, Markwayne Mullin said he was 'turning up the heat'. This is what happens to ICE when you do that," the spokesperson wrote on Wednesday.
Mullin in March became Secretary of Homeland Security.
The Department of Peace said it accessed the DHS agent profiles through a single sign-on service called Okta.
Okta is a popular online security tool that organisations use to ensure that only people with access to internal platforms are logging on to them.
A spokeswoman for Okta said the company is aware of the claims being made, but said: "Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised."
Last month, the FBI was hacked by a group called ShinyHunters, which took personal information about thousands of agents.
In recent days, the Federal Election Commission, which makes public political campaign donation data, was taken offline because of a suspected hacking attempt.

Public backlash to US immigration enforcement has been building as the Trump Administration has pushed a huge increase in arrests and deportations of people suspected of being in the country illegally.
Immigration operations this year have repeatedly turned violent, external, with ICE agents shooting at more than two dozen people and killing at least nine people.
Those killings include the high profile deaths of Alex Pretti and Renee Good, both of whom were shot and killed by ICE agents this year in Minnesota, despite not being the targets of arrests.

Often, ICE agents carry out enforcement actions while their faces are covered by masks and sunglasses. Immigration agents rarely identify themselves, despite being required by law to do so, and US politicians have publicly demanded, external DHS enforces the requirement.

Since President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025, the US has enacted nearly 1 million deportations, external, according to data from the Migration Policy Institute. More than 70% of the deportations have been of people with no criminal record.

articles.headline: BioWare Co-Founder Says EA’s Private Equity Acquisition Was ‘Final Nail In The Coffin’ For The Mass Effect Studio
keyFacts: BioWare co-founder Greg Zeschuk stated that EA's private equity acquisition was the final nail in the coffin for the studio.
Zeschuk expressed concern for current staff being pushed into a hostile job market after the studio's recent closure.
Zeschuk disputed claims that BioWare was failing before its original 2007 acquisition, stating the studio was in good shape and seeking funding.
body: BioWare co-founders Greg Zeschuk and Ray Muzyka chose the (relatively?) quiet life when they retired from the Mass Effect studio in 2012 a few months after the launch of Mass Effect 3. Though the pair hadnât been part of the company in over a decade, naturally, people might be interested to hear what they had to say about the studioâs closure last week under publisher EA and its new private equity owners. Zeschuk did his first interview following the end of the company he founded in 1995, and says that he had already mourned BioWare when he left the Edmonton developer 14 years ago. But he still had thoughts on how it all went down.
âI’ve kind of gone through all the emotions like long, long ago,â Zeschuk told 80.lv. âYou have to break from it and kind of go, âOkay, I’ve had my emotional moment.ââ

While he may have felt more detached after years of distance, he was still concerned for the people who were still at BioWare, and lamented that his old colleagues and people on the team he never worked with were being pushed out into a hostile job market.

You can read the full interview for more of Zeschukâs insight on how BioWareâs ability to put out games, even ones that werenât as revered as its pre-Andromeda output, was still âa successâ in that the studio was able to work within EAâs âframework.â But some of the more interesting parts of the interview are where Zeschuk reflects on BioWareâs original 2007 acquisition and whether or not he regrets it.Â

Though there has been some conjecture that BioWare was in danger of going under if not for the EA acquisition, Zeschuk disputes that, and says that the studio was âin good shape,â and that the company was looking for a means to secure more funding for the Star Wars MMO The Old Republic that was in development at the BioWare Austin office.
