articles.headline: 'He could be happier' - why is Estevao becoming Chelsea's forgotten man?
keyFacts: Chelsea forward Estevao has struggled for playing time and failed to start a Premier League match under manager Xabi Alonso this season.
Alonso stated that Estevao is adapting to the physical demands of English football and will eventually get his opportunity to play.
Pedro Neto's strong form in Estevao's preferred right-sided position has further limited the Brazilian player's opportunities under the current system.
body: - Published
The last time Chelsea beat Liverpool, Estevao was the talk of the Premier League.

The Brazilian was still in his first couple of months at Stamford Bridge when his name hit the headlines after he scored the winner against the Premier League champions with practically the final kick of the match last October.
Fast forward 12 months, and Estevao is beginning to attract attention for all the wrong reasons as he struggles to force his way into Xabi Alonso's side.

The 19-year-old, who joined Chelsea from Palmeiras last summer, was conspicuous by his absence on Wednesday night as Chelsea were knocked out of the Carabao Cup following a penalty shootout loss to Liverpool at Anfield.
The Blues had taken the lead in the first half through Morgan Rogers, but they failed to kick on after Cody Gakpo quickly restored parity for the hosts.
Most concerning for Estevao, though, was that as both teams pushed for a winner in the second half, Alonso never appeared to consider the forward.

The clearest indication of just how low Estevao sits in Alonso's pecking order came midway through the second half, when Alonso made a triple substitution in an attempt to turn the game in his side's favour.
One of the three changes was Emanuel Emegha, who had yet to feature for the Blues since his summer move from Strasbourg.
Just moments after that triple change, which brought Chelsea's total number of substitutions to five, Estevao could be seen ending his warm-up and retreating to the bench.
It was another night of no action for the Brazilian.
'I'm sure Estevao will have his moment'
Sadly for Estevao, Wednesday night's situation at Anfield was nothing new for him.
The Brazilian has failed to make the starting XI in any of the eight Premier League matches since Alonso took charge of the Blues in the summer.
His total minutes for the campaign so far stand at an underwhelming 172, with 125 of those coming in the victories over Luton Town and Leeds United in the earlier rounds of the EFL Cup.
Yet even in the thrilling 6-3 win against Daniel Farke's side, which remains one of only two games he has started this campaign, he was withdrawn at half-time with Chelsea trailing 1-0.
After the fourth-round defeat by Liverpool, Alonso defended his decision not to play Estevao, hinting that the forward is still coming to grips with the physical demands of English football.
"We started with Pedro [Neto], Morgan [Rogers] and Danny Welbeck, and the game had very intense moments," said Alonso.
"We knew it was going to be physical, and Malo [Gusto] had cramps, so we were a bit forced with substitutions. The season is going to be very long, and there will be moments for everyone."
When asked directly about the Brazilian, Alonso added: "He could be happier. He wants to play. I'm sure Estevao will have his moment, it is my responsibility.
"We know the game in England is really intense, and you need to be up for it. Estevao is in his second season. The season is going to be long."
Neto's revival and attacking firepower limit Estevao's chances
One of the main reasons behind Estevao's exile has been the form of Pedro Neto.
It was only a couple of months ago that Portugal international Neto looked destined to leave Chelsea, only two years after joining from Wolverhampton Wanderers.
The 26-year-old was linked with a move to Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli, but he ultimately remained at Stamford Bridge.
That decision appears to have been influenced by Alonso, who has underlined his faith in Neto by handing him seven starts in eight Premier League matches this season.
His success out on the right - which also happens to be Estevao's favoured position - has meant opportunities have been few and far between for the Brazilian.

He has primarily been deployed as a right-sided wing-back in Alonso's 3-4-2-1 system, with his Premier League experience and greater defensive solidity compared to Estevao seemingly winning over the Spaniard.
After an impressive start to the campaign, in which he has scored four goals in 11 matches, Neto was rewarded with a new six-year deal at Stamford Bridge.
"He's a player who is a little bit of a victim of the system," former Reading midfielder Jobi McAnuff told Sky Sports.
"Alonso tends to play Neto in that hybrid wing-back role, expecting him to get high up the pitch as well. Maybe he doesn't feel that suits Estevao, and I don't feel it does either."

One area that has not been a problem for the Blues this season is attack, with the forward positions firmly in the hands of Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Rogers, who has made a spectacular start to life at Stamford Bridge following his Â£117m move from Aston Villa.
Against Liverpool, though, Estevao couldn't even get a look-in despite Chelsea being without the suspended Palmer and the injured Joao Pedro.
"How Estevao has not got on the pitch tonight, I do not know," said former Crystal Palace forward Clinton Morrison.
"He must be thinking, 'What do I have to do? We have injuries to two of the star players up front, and I'm still not getting on the pitch'."
Estevao will be hoping he can follow in the footsteps of Neto and revive his Stamford Bridge career.

articles.headline: You Can Spend Nearly $15K on Apple’s New Touchscreen MacBook Pro. Why?
keyFacts: Apple announced the new touchscreen MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR Display, starting at $2,899 and launching on November 6.
Fully upgrading the 16-inch model with maximum memory and storage raises the price to $14,549.
CNET editors stated that these expensive top-tier configurations are primarily purchased by companies and institutions rather than individual consumers.
body: The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, announced on Wednesday and available on Nov. 6, brings touchscreen control to Apple’s most premium laptop. Pricing starts at $2,899 for the entry-level M5 Pro with the smaller 14-inch display, or $3,399 for the 16-inch model, before any applicable education discounts.

If you go ham on Apple’s preorder configurator and max out the processor, memory and storage, the price balloons to an eye-watering $14,549. That’s wild, especially in today’s economy. Will anyone actually spend that?
Fully loading the M5 MacBook Pro

Let’s see what it means to reach that top-tier configuration of the new touchscreen laptop, starting with the larger, more expensive 16-inch PROLED XDR model at $3,399. Color doesn’t affect price, so take your pick of silver or space black.
More from CNET
The first upgrade you’ll pay for is Nano-texture glass, an antireflective glass finish physically etched at the nanometer scale to diffuse ambient light and eliminate glare, for an additional $150.

Then, stepping up from the M5 Pro’s 20-core GPU to the M5 Max’s 35-core GPU brings the total to $4,949. Bumping to the even more potent 40-core GPU adds another $300, while unlocking horsepower for complex tasks like gaming, video editing and AI-driven operations such as machine learning and coding. (In our testing, CNET found that the Max 40-core is the best fit for pro creatives who work with 8K or raw video, data scientists and intensive users of generative AI imaging and video.)

Next comes memory and storage, which is where things get really expensive. Our starting M5 Max configuration comes standard with 48GB of unified memory and 2TB of storage, but we can pump those numbers considerably. Upgrading to 128GB of memory adds $2,000. Going for 16TB of storage adds $7,000, the most expensive upgrade on the list, roughly doubling the price of the machine.
Pricey high-capacity memory and storage were par for the course long before the RAMpocalypse, but the current AI-fueled spike in RAM and solid-state storage prices has made things worse.

“It’s so expensive because 16TB drives cost a fortune, as does 128GB, and professionals have been paying those workstation prices for years,” Lori Grunin, CNET senior editor for computers and gaming hardware, told me.

Maxing the RAM boosts bandwidth and performance, allowing the Mac to more easily work with the massive files used in high-resolution video, complex 3D models, large datasets and complex mathematical equations. The extra terabytes of storage mean more and larger files can be saved to the device, since neither the MacBook’s memory nor storage can be upgraded after purchase.
All in, our fully loaded MacBook Pro M5 Max with 16-inch PROLED XDR Display comes to $14,549.
Grunin said she’d want more for the money. “For that price, I’d expect the M5 Ultra chip,” she said. “But I don’t think they can put the Ultra in a laptop yet.”
These upgrades aren’t for everyday people
So who buys a laptop that costs more than a used car? Is this just a flex for the super-rich?
“It’s for people who don’t have to pay for it,” said CNET Managing Editor Joshua Goldman.

Configured-to-order, powerful mobile workstations like these are most commonly bought through enterprise procurement by companies, startups and institutions — so the employer is paying, not the individual. Think engineering and architecture firms, Hollywood VFX and post-production houses or AI, machine learning and data science teams. They have big budgets, can put the extra digital horsepower to use and can easily absorb the exorbitant price.
For context, Grunin pointed me to a Dell Precision workstation that I was able to trick out to over $18,000. Five-figure enterprise-scale machines from HP or Lenovo are also not out of the question.

Yes, there will be well-heeled individuals buying at this level, but they’re a relatively small slice of the pie. More likely, the majority of the new touch-enabled MacBook Pros sold will be at still-expensive but easier-to-fathom prices.

articles.headline: Upwind raises $400M after walking away from Datadog acquisition offer
keyFacts: Cloud security startup Upwind raised a $400 million Series C round at a $3.8 billion valuation led by Bessemer Venture Partners.
Upwind decided to remain independent after rejecting an acquisition offer from Datadog that did not exceed the venture capital valuation, according to a source.
Upwind is projected to reach approximately $90 million in annualized recurring revenue by the end of the year, according to a financial source.
body: Upwind, a San Francisco startup that uses AI to secure cloud infrastructure, has raised a $400 million Series C round at a $3.8 billion valuation led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from existing backers including Greylock Partners and Craft Ventures.
The round comes nine months after Upwind closed its previous $250 million financing at a $1.5 billion valuation.

The fresh funding, which has been in the works for months, nearly fell apart after Datadog attempted to buy the company, according to a person familiar with Upwind. Datadog is a publicly traded company that sells tools for monitoring how software runs, known as observability. It didn’t offer a premium above the $3.8 billion valuation set by venture capital investors, the person said, so Upwind decided to stay independent.

Four-year-old Upwind has grown rapidly amid rising AI-driven cybersecurity threats. The startup has been adding $20 million to $30 million in annualized recurring revenue (ARR) each quarter and is projected to end the year at roughly $90 million, according to a person familiar with Upwind’s financials. That means that VCs and Datadog valued the startup at more than 40 times its forecast ARR, a common yardstick for pricing software companies. The high multiple is also well below the 80x ARR fetched by Cyera, another fast-growing cybersecurity startup, according to TechCrunch reporting from earlier this year.

Cybersecurity is poised to be the third big wave of AI software that companies will pay for after AI coding tools and customer support, Theory Ventures general partner Tomasz Tunguz recently wrote in his widely read blog.

By walking away from an acquisition offer, Upwind clearly believes that the company will ultimately be worth more than the $3.8 billion that Datadog was ready to pay for it. However, given how few cybersecurity companies have gone public in recent years, an eventual sale remains the most likely outcome for the startup.
Upwind continues to draw acquisition interest, according to a person familiar with the company.

The startup was founded by Amiram Shachar, who sold his previous company, the cloud spend management startup Spot.io, to NetApp for $450 million. Upwind calls its approach to thwarting threats “runtime” security, which means it alerts and remedies attacks and vulnerabilities in active services in real time.
TechCrunch has reached out to both Upwind and Datadog for comment.

articles.headline: FCC chair wants to let prisons jam illegal cellphones
keyFacts: The US Federal Communications Commission announced it will vote next month on a new rule allowing state prisons to use cellphone jammers.
The proposed policy aims to block inmates from using illegal cellphones to engage in criminal activity.
The agency will vote on the matter during its open meeting scheduled for November 19.
body: FCC chair wants to let prisons jam illegal cellphones
The agency will vote next month on relaxing its long-standing opposition to jammers.

The US Federal Communications Commission announced today that it will vote on a new rule that would allow state prisons and jails to use cellphone jammers. The goal of the change would be to block use of illegal cellphones by inmates, since having outside contact could allow them to continue engaging in criminal activity.

The planned vote during the agency's open meeting on November 19 would consider allowing state and local incarceration facilities to opt in to using jammers; use of the tech would not be required. Any tech that interferes with communications signals is illegal for non-federal parties to use. In 2018, the Federal Bureau of Prisons began testing "micro-jamming" in federal prisons as a way to block unauthorized cellphone use by inmates. This move would potentially open up similar tools at the state and local levels, and provide a formal pathway for federal facilities to jam signals as well.

It's a reversal from previous policies where the FCC has not allowed implementing jammers as a method of reducing illegal cellphone use in prisons. Previous concerns about jammers suggested the tech could interfere with emergency and public safety communications, as well as creating new security risks by putting more jamming tools into the wild where they could be exploited by bad actors. The bulletin today notes that if the new rules are adopted, correctional facilities would need to meet some standards, including proving "that the jamming solution does not cause harmful interference outside of the designated geographic areas."

Today's move isn't the first time the FCC has changed its approach toward prisons under the current administration. In July 2025, the department said it would delay implementing a cap on the rates charged for prison phone calls.

articles.headline: ULA's Vulcan rocket is set to return to flight on Friday the 13th
keyFacts: United Launch Alliance announced it will return its Vulcan rocket to flight on November 13 to launch 40 satellites for Amazon.
The mission follows a nine-month grounding after solid rocket booster nozzle failures occurred during two of the rocket's first four flights.
US Space Force officials will closely monitor the launch because the Pentagon relies on the Vulcan rocket for major national security missions.
body: United Launch Alliance announced Wednesday it plans to return its Vulcan rocket to service on November 13, nine months after a solid rocket booster anomaly threw the company’s 2026 launch schedule into oblivion.

The return-to-flight mission will launch 40 satellites for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation, the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon has booked to deploy the bulk of its network. The mission will lift off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, and ULA said the launch date is pending range approval.

The launch is critical for ULA after its new flagship rocket suffered nozzle failures on its solid rocket boosters on two of its first four missions, most recently during a flight in February. In both cases, the rocket overcame the nozzle failure and completed its mission, but officials at the US Space Force, ULA’s primary customer, lost confidence in Vulcan.

Space Force officials will closely scrutinize Vulcan’s return-to-flight mission. The Pentagon has entrusted ULA’s Vulcan rocket for roughly half of its major launches through the early 2030s. The Space Force certified the Vulcan rocket for national security launches in 2025, then flew two missions on Vulcan before its grounding after the February booster incident.
Making strides

In a statement, United Launch Alliance said engineers “made great strides” in understanding the booster anomaly that occurred in February. Engineers “have identified several potential contributors, which have been mitigated through design and process improvements to the nozzle,” ULA said.

“To support our customers, this upcoming launch will utilize the improved nozzle design, and additional testing and analysis will continue in parallel with the mission,” ULA said. “By flying the improved design, ULA gains valuable flight data that validates these improvements and is the most beneficial path in support of all our customers.”

articles.headline: Kompany discharged from hospital after collapsing at training
keyFacts: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has been discharged from hospital after collapsing during training due to a meningeal irritation, board member Max Eberl said.
Eberl stated that Kompany will rest and take medication, while assistant Aaron Danks noted that no return date has been set.
Assistant coach Aaron Danks continues to lead the team in Kompany's absence while prioritising his recovery and health.
body: Vincent Kompany: Bayern Munich head coach discharged from hospital after collapsing at training

Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany has been discharged from hospital, says board member for sports Max Eberl; the former Man City defender collapsed during a second-team training session on Friday; Kompany had missed some duties earlier in the week due to a viral infection
Wednesday 28 October 2026 23:08, UK

Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has been discharged from hospital following his collapse in training last week due to a meningeal irritation, board member for sports Max Eberl said on Wednesday.
Kompany was taken to hospital last week after collapsing at Bayern's training ground during a second-team training session.
He missed out on media duties ahead of Bayern's Champions League match against Arsenal due to a viral infection, but did make it to the dugout for the 2-2 draw.

"Given the circumstances, he's doing well," Eberl told broadcaster ARD ahead of the German Cup game against Magdeburg, who Bayern beat 6-1. "He was discharged from the hospital today [Wednesday]. That is the biggest and best news for all of us.
"It's a meningeal irritation that caused this incident on Friday. He will now rest and take medication and I am certain that he will very soon be back on the touchline, operating at 100 per cent."
No date has been set for Kompany's return, with Eberl saying the Belgian would resume his duties only after receiving medical clearance, something that was reiterated by his assistant, Aaron Danks.
Speaking after the win against Magdeburg, he said: "I still don't feel like there is any timeline on it [when Kompany is back]. It's obviously a really positive step in his road to recovery.

"He gets to settle back at home now, be closer to his family, be closer to his home comforts but it's still really important that he takes his rest and he recovers. So there is no timescale on it. Nothing that I've been told and I've been informed.
"Our doctors will continue to work closely with Vince and at the right moment, he will be back with us once he is fit and healthy to do that and we look forward to that day.
"But in the meantime, we just continue to push forward as a group with the players and staff and keep working hard.
"I haven't spoken to him for a couple of days now so I still think not much has changed in terms of our working relationship at the moment.
"His health is our number one priority and for us he is still in recovery mode so we want him to get back to full health, full fitness and then join us.
"Over the coming days, weeks, I don't know, things will start to move forward and we can start to engage in more of these conversations.
"But there has been no timescale on that at the moment. It is just purely about his health, his recovery and him taking the time that he needs."
Danks has taken charge of the team and was on the bench for their 3-1 win at Freiburg at the weekend. Bundesliga leaders Bayern face title rivals Borussia Dortmund on Saturday.

articles.headline: Brazilian political drama unfolds as defeated Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami
keyFacts: Defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami following his election loss to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
Brazilian authorities ordered Bolsonaro to surrender his passport because he is facing multiple investigations, including money laundering.
Analyst Fábio Zanini said Bolsonaro plans to stay in the United States and portray himself as a victim of political persecution.
body: Brazilian political drama unfolds as defeated Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami

Defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family have arrived in the U.S. after Brazilian authorities ordered him to surrender his passport. He is facing multiple investigations in Brazil.
JUANA SUMMERS, HOST:

This morning, Brazilians were glued to their screens watching a private plane land at an airport in Miami, Florida. Moments later, the man who had just lost Brazil's presidential election, Flávio Bolsonaro, stepped out onto the tarmac. His arrival capped three days of political drama since his stunning defeat to incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. NPR South America correspondent Carrie Kahn is on the line now. Hey, Carrie.
CARRIE KAHN, BYLINE: Hi.
SUMMERS: So, Carrie, I want to make sure I understand this correctly. Bolsonaro lost Sunday's election, and by Wednesday, he was in the U.S.?

KAHN: Yes, it's been a wild ride the past three days. On Sunday, he refused to concede the election and said he would petition to annul the results. The next day, his party did accept the results. And in a video, Bolsonaro seemed to back down a bit but added that federal police demanded his passport after he was visiting his father, who is under house arrest for attempting to overturn his own electoral loss to Lula four years ago. By Tuesday - yesterday - rumors were flying that Bolsonaro had fled Brazil, and today he arrived in Miami and then later put out a statement first declaring himself as, quote, "the true elected president of Brazil." Then a bit later, he posted a new statement downgrading himself to the true elected leader of Brazil. He compared himself to liberation figures like Charles de Gaulle and María Corina Machado of Venezuela, amongst others.
SUMMERS: Interesting. OK, lots of questions here. One is this - do we know how he managed to leave Brazil and get to the U.S.?

KAHN: Argentine officials reported he crossed into the country last night, but Brazilian officials say they have no record of him crossing. Bolsonaro also has an Italian passport. From Argentina, he flew to Ecuador and then on to Miami. And in his letter today, he thanked Argentina's president, Javier Milei, for his support. And Milei is a far-right ally of Bolsonaro and Trump. And like Trump, Milei has still not recognized Brazil's election results. Trump was asked just a little while ago what he thought of Bolsonaro declaring himself leader of Brazil. Trump said he wasn't going to comment on that.
SUMMERS: Got it. Why did Brazil's federal police revoke his passport?

KAHN: That order came from a Supreme Court justice who said Bolsonaro was a flight risk because he's facing several investigations, and that justice oversaw the case against Bolsonaro's father, Jair. In his letter today, Flávio said that Brazil's judiciary has been, quote, "weaponized" against his entire family. The cases against Bolsonaro include a money laundering scheme tied to online gambling. Another involves questionable financing of a biopic about his father. Bolsonaro denies any wrongdoing.
SUMMERS: And people in Brazil, what have they had to say about his sudden departure?

KAHN: As you can imagine, the country has been captivated. You know, look, the election was decisive for Lula, but nearly 60 million people voted for Bolsonaro and his conservative movement. I spoke with Fábio Zanini, a political columnist with Folha, a newspaper in São Paulo, who says Flávio's departure could help that movement.

FÁBIO ZANINI: Flávio will be in the United States now, close to the Trump administration, attacking Brazil, saying that he's a persecuted person and trying to portray himself as a victim of Brazilian persecution. That might give a new energy to the Bolsonarista movement.

KAHN: Many also say that claims of election tampering and political persecution are pretty hollow because Bolsonaro's party did make huge gains throughout the country. His stepmother and his brother were elected senators, and the party has now the largest majority in Congress.
SUMMERS: NPR's Carrie Kahn, thank you.
KAHN: You're welcome.

articles.headline: Dem AG’s ‘too many golf courses’ remark goes viral as critics tee off
keyFacts: Arizona Democratic Attorney General Kris Mayes faced backlash after saying the state probably has too many golf courses.
Republican State Senator Warren Petersen and business leaders criticized Mayes, citing the golf industry's economic impact and job contributions.
Mayes later responded that nobody is closing golf courses, insisting her remarks were about water conservation incentives.
body: Arizona’s Senate president took aim at viral comments about the future of golf from the state’s Democratic attorney general as their battle to be the state’s top law enforcement officer entered its final stretch before next week’s midterm elections.

A remark about potentially restricting golf courses and the Grand Canyon State having "too much grass" turned a debate over water conservation into a campaign flashpoint, with Sen. Warren Petersen accusing Attorney General Kris Mayes of targeting a multibillion-dollar industry in the desert state while Mayes later insisted her remarks were taken out of context.

"Kris Mayes thinks Arizona has too many golf courses. I think Arizona has too many radical politicians who believe government should dictate which industries get to thrive," Petersen, R-Maricopa, told Fox News Digital Tuesday.
100 DAYS UNTIL MIDTERMS AND DEMOCRATS ARE WINNING BECAUSE THEY ACTUALLY HAVE A MESSAGE

"Our golf courses support jobs, tourism, small businesses and communities across this state. Instead of attacking an industry that contributes to our economy, the attorney general should be focused on enforcing the law, protecting consumers and defending Arizona families."

In an interview with Politico delving into the data center debate and whether the proliferation of water-intensive buildings is wise, particularly in an arid state, Mayes cited neighboring states allegedly "backed by" the Trump administration as hindrances to Arizona’s local supply.
Mayes' golf course remarks came shortly after she warned that Arizona was headed toward a potential Supreme Court showdown over Colorado River water supplies .
"We could do a hell of a lot more when it comes to conservation," she said, citing tax incentives for catchment and removal of lawns.
GRAND CANYON WATER PIPELINE DAMAGED AGAIN AS FLOODING COMPLICATES REPAIRS

"We have way, way too much grass in Arizona. We probably, frankly — and I'm sure the golf industry is not going to like this when I say this — we probably have too many golf courses in Arizona right now."
That remark sparked blowback from Petersen and many others.
"We don’t have a golf course problem in Arizona. We have a dumocrat (sic) problem in Arizona," quipped Rep. Eli Crane, R-Ariz.
"Kris Mayes is promising to get rid of golf courses. I promise to get rid of Kris Mayes," Petersen added in his own tweet.
E-procurement software CEO Tom Spengler added that Arizona "honestly need[s] more golf courses."
"Tee times are very hard to get and rates have doubled or tripled since COVID," he said.
"We have too much grass — said no one ever, other than Kris Mayes," added Turning Point USA executive Justin Streiff.
Arizona’s business community also took notice, and Arizona Chamber of Commerce Vice President Courtney Coolidge responded to Mayes with several statistics about golf’s impact on the state.

Coolidge reported a $6 billion economic impact, 66,000 jobs, $2.3 billion in wages and $520 million in tax revenue. Most relevant to the water debate, she said golf courses collectively use 2% or less of the state’s water resources.
Those stats also lined up closely with separate figures in a 2023 study by the Arizona Alliance for Golf .
Popular golf satire site PGA Tuor shared a clip of Mayes’ comments, writing, "How to not get re-elected 101."
Another putting enthusiast said Mayes’ comments cost her his vote, saying, "[She] has no idea what the economic impact golf has on our entire state."
Fox News Digital reached out to Mayes for comment on the viral nature and content of her remarks.
The Democrat separately tweeted that she was intending to make a larger point about water usage.
"Relax, nobody's closing golf courses," Mayes said.

"My point is we need incentives to help all Arizonans and major industries swap thirsty grass and catch rainwater, especially if our water situation gets worse — while I take on the foreign mega-farms and data centers draining our water."
She then accused Petersen of spreading "false claims."
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

But Mayes’ response was also met with ridicule. X critics called it "condescending" while one also quipped, "you relax – we all heard you." Others characterized her stated approach toward the golf industry as "communist."

With Election Day just days away, Petersen is betting the controversy will resonate beyond the fairways, casting Mayes' remarks as part of a larger dispute over government intervention in Arizona's economy as Republicans seek to regain control of a state government they once reliably held.

articles.headline: Epic Games further doubles down on gen-AI tools for Fortnite, Unreal Engine 6 and more: "Our engineers are no longer writing the bulk of the code"
keyFacts: Epic Games executive Marcus Wassmer confirmed that the company is using generative AI to develop code for Fortnite, Unreal Editor for Fortnite, and Unreal Engine 6.
Wassmer stated that engineers are no longer writing the bulk of the code, but are guiding AI tools to deliver faster updates with fewer bugs.
Epic Games stated it is more concerned about moving slowly than about AI skepticism, worker job security concerns, plagiarism worries, or environmental impacts.
body: To no one's surprise, Epic Games has now confirmed that it's tripling down on its gen-AI push and will use the controversial tech on everything from Fortnite to the next iteration of its widely-used game development engine, Unreal Engine 6.

Speaking to This Week In Video Games, executive vice president of development Marcus Wassmer confirmed that "we are definitely using AI to develop code and features for Unreal Engine," but that work will also be extended to the engine's next big numbered version. "Almost all development happening right now is being done in the dev streams attached to Fortnite, UEFN [Unreal Editor for Fortnite], and UE6."

When asked specifically if Epic is vibe-coding anything related to Unreal Engine, Wassmer put it plainly: "Yes, we are vibe-coding things. That means our engineers are no longer writing the bulk of the code, but they are still guiding the tools to get the architectural result we want. We're not 'one-shotting' the engine; we're iterating with AI to ship features developers want and keep the engine within the memory, performance, and scalability envelopes." Wassmer claimed the AI tools would help the company push out updates faster and with fewer bugs.
